entries.pullQuote: A classic steakhouse splurge with lake views that make the bill easier to swallow.
entries.blurb: Right on the water at Lake Union, Daniel's Broiler does old-school steak dinners with big cuts and bigger views. Expect a milestone bill, and plan it around sunset if you can.

entries.pullQuote: For the city's best sushi, book the counter and let the chefs decide.
entries.blurb: Skip the waterfront oyster crawl and the fish and chips shops, because the finest seafood in town is at Sushi Kashiba. Shiro Kashiba, who trained under Jiro Ono, opened it at the edge of Pike Place Market in 2015 after leaving his namesake restaurant. Expect impeccable nigiri and a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: Come for weekend brunch, when the room is loud and the bread is crusty.
entries.blurb: Café Campagne has been cooking French comfort food in Post Alley for more than forty years, and the dining room still channels a Paris bistro with old posters and lamps made from wine bottles. Dinner is mellow and the steak frites are great, but brunch is when this place comes alive. Market crowds spill in to share fluffy egg dishes and good bread over upbeat music, and the check lands in special-occasion range.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up, sit at the bar, and order the lamb agnolotti with fries.
entries.blurb: The George brings real glamour to the renovated Fairmont Olympic Hotel, and it's somewhere you can dress up without feeling silly. The menu runs long, from seafood towers to pasta, and not all of it lands, so skip the steak and duck. Go for lamb agnolotti in parmesan broth and a side of fries with some bubbles. Expect a special-occasion bill.

entries.pullQuote: Book the Spheres room when a Roman pizza night should feel like a splurge.
entries.blurb: Renee Erickson's Willmott's Ghost sits inside the Amazon Spheres, a blush-pink room serving Roman-inspired Italian food. Order the Roman-style pizza and pastas, and plan on a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: Book the counter for a parade of nigiri and a seriously special night.
entries.blurb: Sushi by Scratch Restaurants runs an intimate omakase counter in Belltown where chefs work through a long series of creative nigiri right in front of you. It's a special-occasion check, seatings run late, and it's a strong move for impressing visiting parents.

entries.pullQuote: Book a solo seat for the multi-course kaiseki and sushi meal of your year.
entries.blurb: Reservations for two at Taneda are nearly impossible, but single seats open up far more often, and a solo dinner here is a treat rather than a consolation. The meal runs around two dozen courses of sushi and kaiseki in a tiny spot at the back of a Capitol Hill indoor mall. The check is a special-occasion one, yet it is a strong value among the city omakase counters.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the parents here for a Turkish dinner that feels like an occasion.
entries.blurb: For a dressed-up Turkish meal in Phinney Ridge, Ada's Restaurant & Bar carries a special-occasion check that works well with family in tow.

entries.pullQuote: Snag a counter seat for eight courses and a crab nugget you'll crave later.
entries.blurb: From the team behind Shiro's, Shomon gives Seattle omakase a looser, livelier spin. Chefs move around an open kitchen chatting with guests over a mellow lo-fi soundtrack, and the courses mix nigiri with other Japanese small plates, like Hokkaido scallop, futomaki with a soy-cured yolk, and a fried Dungeness crab croquette with béchamel. The counter is roomier than most, and the check lands firmly in special-occasion territory.

entries.pullQuote: Take your parents to Queen Anne for a dressed-up New American dinner.
entries.blurb: Betty Restaurant & Bar runs a special-occasion check on Queen Anne.

entries.pullQuote: Filipino cooking on Beacon Hill worth dressing up for, parents or date in tow.
entries.blurb: Musang turns Filipino food into a full-on celebration on Beacon Hill, and you are paying for the room too. Bring a date or bring the folks, and order plenty to share.

The Capitol Hill dining room mixes reclaimed wood with a sleek marble bar and an open kitchen where you can watch the noodles being made. Expect a special-occasion check, and know the kitchen keeps going late.

entries.pullQuote: A classic special-occasion steakhouse for impressing your parents, ideally on their dime.
entries.blurb: Downtown, The Capital Grille sticks to the dark-wood steakhouse formula with a big check and the polish that parents tend to appreciate.

entries.pullQuote: Save the kaiseki menu for an occasion, and savor the sushi courses most.
entries.blurb: Near the Space Needle, where most restaurants disappoint, wa'z quietly serves an excellent kaiseki menu on beautiful dinnerware. The eight courses change monthly but usually include soup, a generous piece of wagyu, and terrific sushi, often brightened with yuzu and mirin. Flavors lean subtle rather than flashy. It's a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: Book this Denny Triangle dining room when someone else is picking up the check.
entries.blurb: Save 2120 for the night someone else is hosting. The cooking is New American, the room is dressed for a celebration, and Denny Triangle is simply where the table happens to be.

entries.pullQuote: Book it for the skyline views and a dinner that feels like an occasion.
entries.blurb: High up in the Lotte Hotel, Charlotte Restaurant & Lounge pairs New American plates with sweeping views over downtown and the water. The bill belongs to a celebration, so save it for anniversaries and visiting parents who love a view.

entries.pullQuote: Order the stewed pork neck and save serious room for peach cobbler.
entries.blurb: Communion Restaurant & Bar sits in the Liberty Bank Building and cooks like a tribute to both the American South and the Central District around it. Berbere-rubbed chicken over lemony lentils tips its hat to the neighborhood's Ethiopian community, while the pork neck is pure Southern comfort. The bill belongs to a celebration, and the meal earns it.

entries.pullQuote: Book the single nightly seating for a vegan tasting menu worth celebrating.
entries.blurb: Harvest Beat makes the case that a special occasion doesn't need meat or butter. There's one seating each night, kicked off by a gong and a speech from the chef about the farmers and foragers behind dishes like carrot ginger bisque and a cashew paneer loaf. Wine pairing is part of the deal, though the fresh-pressed elixir pairing is the more interesting route, and a berry bread pudding often closes things out with birthday candles.

entries.pullQuote: Start with the seafood pancake and a chili lime martini, then keep ordering.
entries.blurb: Paju traded its cramped Queen Anne home for a much bigger South Lake Union space with a full bar, a wood-fired grill anchoring the open kitchen, and plenty of black marble. The menu grew too, but the reasons to come are the same ones as before. A savory seafood pancake buried in wiggling bonito flakes goes great with the chili lime oil martini, and squid-ink kimchi fried rice comes with bacon. Bring a special-occasion budget.

entries.pullQuote: Save this Madison Valley tasting menu for a milestone dinner worth dressing up.
entries.blurb: Surrell builds a multi-course meal around Pacific Northwest ingredients in an intimate Madison Valley room. This is a dressed-up night, best saved for anniversaries and big celebrations.

It's only open Thursday through Sunday, with à la carte dinners at the start of the stretch and prix fixe on weekends. Expect a special-occasion check and make a reservation.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up, order a dry-aged steak, and let the tableside show unfold.
entries.blurb: Dim lights, live piano, and servers working tableside carts make El Gaucho the old-school supper club Belltown never outgrew. Get a dry-aged cut with a Caesar tossed right in front of you. Bring a fat budget, since this is a special-occasion check through and through.

entries.pullQuote: A Columbia City splurge for a date who appreciates serious cooking.
entries.blurb: Off Alley packs a lot of ambition into a tiny Columbia City room, and this is a dressed-up night that makes sense for a date night.

entries.pullQuote: Book well ahead for a Filipino tasting menu that tells a personal story.
entries.blurb: Archipelago runs a small, story-driven tasting menu that ties Filipino-American history to Pacific Northwest ingredients. Seats are few and the bill is a splurge, so plan a real celebration around it.

entries.pullQuote: Serious omakase without the hush, tucked down an alley in Madison Park.
entries.blurb: Madison Park is all Porsches and pampered dogs, so a back-alley sushi counter fits right in. What surprises is how relaxed Sushi Suzuki feels, a small room squeezed between a bookstore and a salon that could pass for a brewery taproom. The courses are tiny and numerous, the fish does the talking, and the bill is firmly special-occasion.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up and celebrate here, where the lake view does half the work.
entries.blurb: Since the fifties, Canlis has been the city's go-to for big celebrations, set in a mid-century modern house perched above Lake Union. Service is famously polished, the tall windows put the water front and center, and the check matches the occasion. Book it for an anniversary, a proposal, or a parents' visit.

entries.pullQuote: Order both the salmon and tuna samplers, plus a baked crab hand roll.
entries.blurb: A Belltown sushi institution, Shiro's Sushi Restaurant gets everything right, but the samplers are what you will remember. The salmon plate runs through four cuts and preparations, from seared belly to ikura, while the tuna plate shows off lean, marinated, fatty, and negitoro from a single fish. Sit at the counter for omakase at least once, and budget for a special-occasion check.

title: Cheap Eats
dek: The $ tier: counters and small rooms with a humane receipt.
intro:
The $ tier: counters and small rooms with a humane receipt. Bottega Gabriele and Fortuna Bottega prove a good meal does not need a reservation or a second mortgage.

Counters, small rooms, and the kind of receipt you can explain to yourself later. Eat it there. A lot of this food gets worse in a car.

entries.pullQuote: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.
entries.blurb: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.

entries.pullQuote: Get the steamed barbecue pork bao and eat it walking through the stalls.
entries.blurb: Swing by in the late morning, before the market fully wakes up, and you'll catch the crew at Mee Sum Pastry folding potstickers and pinching shumai. Grab an assortment and snack your way through Pike Place. It's all good, but the steamed pork hum bao is the order regulars make, and it's open early and inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: New England clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl, with oyster crackers, in Post Alley.
entries.blurb: Get the clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl and add oyster crackers. Skip the smoked salmon chowder.

entries.pullQuote: Get the beef and cheese, eat it standing up, and don't mind the line.
entries.blurb: Since the early nineties, Piroshky Piroshky has filled the market with the smell of baked Russian hand pies, both savory and sweet. The line moves faster than it looks, prices stay friendly, and the counter opens early enough to make breakfast out of a smoked salmon pastry.

entries.pullQuote: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.
entries.blurb: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.

entries.pullQuote: Bacon, egg and cheese on a poppy seed bagel.
entries.blurb: The Good Shape Pizza team turned its attention to sandwiches at Louie's Deli, a royal blue counter in Pioneer Square. Sesame hoagie rolls are crunchy and chewy, bacon is chopped into small bits, and cold cuts are shaved impossibly thin. The bacon, egg and cheese is on a poppy seed bagel. There's an arcade room next door for pinball after lunch.

entries.pullQuote: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.
entries.blurb: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.

entries.pullQuote: Come in with friends or solo, best turkey sandwich around.
entries.blurb: Come in with friends or solo, best turkey sandwich around.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Thanksgiving turkey sandwich and add tater tots for dunking.
entries.blurb: Valhalla Sandwiches in Greenwood manages to go big without getting sloppy. The sandwiches come on sturdy telera rolls with fillings like blackened shrimp and chorizo, chicken with sweet-hot mustard and slaw, or turkey with stuffing, cranberry, and rosemary aioli. Tater tots with chipotle mayo are a must, and the whole thing is inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.
entries.blurb: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.

entries.pullQuote: The bacon-beef burger and herby shoestring fries are worth earning with a hike.
entries.blurb: Patties topped with special sauce, sharp aged cheddar, sweet onions, and thick-cut pickles are the headliners at Big Max Burger Co. The Nashville-style hot chicken sandwich, glazed with smoky chili and served with plenty of ranch, is just as good. Round things out with a milkshake, kettle corn brussels sprouts, or puffy chicken nuggets and sweet and sour sauce.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap toasted subs that hit hardest when it's late and you're starving.
entries.blurb: A stoner-themed chain counter near the university, Cheba Hut Toasted Subs keeps the oven running late and the prices low.

entries.pullQuote: Brave the line of tourists for a cup of that famous mac and cheese.
entries.blurb: The nutty, sharp Flagship cheddar from Beecher's Handmade Cheese is in every grocery store in town, but the Pike Place Market shop is where it all gets made. Expect a line packed with curd-sampling tourists at lunch. The reward is a creamy mac and cheese that once made Oprah's list of favorite things, and it's inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: A no-fuss Fremont counter for a cheap burger without a reservation.
entries.blurb: Walk in, order at the counter, and Uneeda Burger will hand you an inexpensive burger in Fremont.

entries.pullQuote: Come for the wings, stay for the chaos, and catch the game if you must.
entries.blurb: Vindicktive Wings looks like a generic Belltown sports bar at first, all big booths and TVs, but people show up here for wings first and the game second. Give it time and the room starts to feel like a great college party, with loud music and bartenders who remember you. The wings are inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: Eat a double cheeseburger and a root beer float in the car.
entries.blurb: For a double cheeseburger with fries and a shake on pocket change, Pick-Quick Drive In has you covered. The burgers beat Dick's handily, and you get to sit down while you eat them. Load your friends into the car and get everyone root beer floats made with real soft serve.

entries.pullQuote: A Deluxe, fries, and a chocolate shake is a Seattle rite of passage.
entries.blurb: Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

entries.pullQuote: Griddled corned beef with mint and pickled cabbage, from a Momofuku alum.
entries.blurb: Order the Mean: thick griddled corned beef, house yellow mustard, pickled red cabbage and fresh mint on a challah bun. It comes with the salt-and-pepper potato skins.

entries.pullQuote: Lower Queen Anne karaoke, priced like a dive, and open until 2.
entries.blurb: Ozzie's is a Lower Queen Anne dive with karaoke and an American kitchen, and the lights stay on until 2. Prices sit at the cheap end on purpose. Pick a song you can finish, stand where people will clap, and skip the night if nobody in the group will sing. A plainer pub can sell you a beer anywhere on Queen Anne. This room only earns the walk once the microphone is switched on.

entries.pullQuote: Order the adobada tacos with grilled pineapple and you've made the right call.
entries.blurb: The Broadway taco counter in a building shared with a tattoo shop stopped being a secret long ago, and Tacos Chukis earned the crowds. The house adobada tacos stack marinated grilled pork with avocado salsa, cilantro, onion, and a seared slab of pineapple. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, and it's an ideal stop before a night out.

entries.pullQuote: Fine for a patio break with visitors, but skip the pricey crab.
entries.blurb: Up at the north end of Pike Place, Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder caters to tourists with a menu that comes and goes in quality. The fried fish is fine, and the bacon-y clam chowder with its Goldfish-style crackers is the strongest play. A breezy patio over Elliott Bay makes it a decent rest stop with guests.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap downtown hot dog when lunch needs to happen in five minutes.
entries.blurb: Dog in the Park handles quick, inexpensive franks for Downtown lunch breaks.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap Italian sandwiches in Greenwood, no reservation needed, just show up hungry.
entries.blurb: Fortuna Bottega makes inexpensive Italian sandwiches at a walk-up Greenwood counter.

entries.pullQuote: Order more empanadas than you think you need, especially the creamed spinach.
entries.blurb: Over in Ballard, Maria Luisa Empanadas turns out tender pastries stuffed with meats, cheeses, and vegetables, plus a chimichurri you'll want to bottle. The garage-style room has high-tops for a quick lunch, and takeout is easy even for a crowd. Picking a favorite is hard, but the creamed spinach and the tangy chorizo lead the pack.

entries.pullQuote: The corned beef reuben here is the benchmark for every deli in town.
entries.blurb: Look for the huge corned beef sign over the Denny Triangle and you've found Market House Meats. The shop has fed office workers and early construction crews since the forties, and the griddle is always sizzling. That tender, salty corned beef goes into a reuben you'll measure every other one against. It's inexpensive, quick, and open early.

entries.pullQuote: Get the Italian sub, add a breakfast sandwich, and bring patience.
entries.blurb: The owners once ran Lyon's Grocery in Queen Anne, and that pedigree shows in every sandwich at Otherside Market & Deli in Eastlake. The Italian sub piles on ham with pepperoncini and a hit of red wine vinegar, while breakfast sandwiches arrive gooey on Backyard bagels. Even a plain turkey and cheese on wheat is great here.

entries.pullQuote: This gluten-free Filipino fried chicken is crispier than nearly anything else in town.
entries.blurb: The Chicken Supply dredges its Filipino fried chicken in tapioca, rice flour, and potato starch, and that celiac-friendly coating is exactly why it's so good. Thigh skin crackles like a chip, and the skewers of white meat stay remarkably juicy. Seating is limited to a handful of tables in the small Phinney Ridge room. Prices stay pleasantly low.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap Central District burger fix you can grab at the counter.
entries.blurb: Inexpensive burgers from a casual counter make Ox Burger an easy Central District stop.

entries.pullQuote: Get onion rings to dunk in fry sauce, plus a mint truffle shake.
entries.blurb: Nobody comes to Red Mill Burgers for gourmet toppings or atmosphere. You come for a charbroiled diner-style patty, cornmeal-crusted onion rings dunked in fry sauce, and a thick shake in flavors like s'mores. Grab a spot at one of the bright red picnic tables, ideally after a hike or a slow afternoon around Phinney Ridge.

entries.pullQuote: Order the chicken caesar wrap, then come back another day for the reuben.
entries.blurb: Take 5 Urban Market has the Moon Pies and fruit sodas of a proper corner store, plus a short sandwich menu that deserves real attention. The reuben swaps kraut for creamy slaw and gets a crisp layer of griddled swiss, and the sriracha chicken melt brings plenty of avocado and actual heat. Still, the one you will crave is the chicken caesar, packed with bacon, tomato, and crouton bits.

entries.pullQuote: Pay the extra few bucks for halibut and eat it near the beach.
entries.blurb: Alki Spud Fish and Chips has been frying seafood by the beach since the thirties, and old photos and maps of West Seattle cover the walls to prove it. The halibut costs a little more and is absolutely the order, flaky and tender under a crisp, well-seasoned batter. Portions can run huge, and it all comes cheap enough when midday has to be fast or a visit with out-of-town guests.

entries.pullQuote: Come for the empanadas and leave with a box of alfajores for later.
entries.blurb: This Lake City counter is among the few places in Seattle specializing in Argentine baked goods, from dulce de leche alfajores to glossy medialunas and quince pastafrola. Still, the empanadas are why Seatangofoods deserves a lunch detour, golden and often fresh out of the oven. Lake City can get an empanada before the commute, which is the practical glory here.

entries.pullQuote: Thick handmade tortillas and that chorizo, potato, and cactus filling are the move.
entries.blurb: Carmelo's Tacos presses its own hefty tortillas and fills them with well-marinated carne asada or a chorizo, potato, and nopal mix that sticks with you. Burrito people should know the cheese gets a quick sear on the griddle before it goes in. It's cheap, it's fast, and the Capitol Hill counter keeps going late.

entries.pullQuote: Pick a heat level one notch below your ego and order the sliders.
entries.blurb: Nashville-style hot chicken tenders and sliders make up nearly the whole menu at Dave's Hot Chicken, with spice that runs from mild to genuinely painful. The Capitol Hill counter keeps it cheap.

entries.pullQuote: The Fairfax on a warm brioche bun fixes almost any rough morning.
entries.blurb: The LA egg sandwich chain Eggslut landed on Capitol Hill, and the Fairfax, with soft scrambled eggs, chives, cheddar, and sriracha mayo on a brioche bun, is the order regulars make. Doors open early, and the bill stays gentle enough for a weekday treat.

entries.pullQuote: Get a mozzarella dog, add sugar and ketchup, and don't overthink it.
entries.blurb: Korean-style corn dogs in a crisp rice-flour batter are the specialty at Chung Chun Rice Dog, including cheesy and potato-studded versions. It's an inexpensive snack stop in the Chinatown-International District.

entries.pullQuote: The grilled pork bánh mì here is still a cheap lunch miracle.
entries.blurb: Prices creep up everywhere, but Saigon Viet Nam Deli in the International District still sells a bánh mì that barely dents your wallet. The grilled pork version comes on crackly fresh bread with a generous swipe of bơ and plenty of coarse black pepper. It tastes the same every time, which is the highest compliment.

entries.pullQuote: Order the salmon sinigang, follow the signs, and don't rush the cook.
entries.blurb: In a quiet corner of Pike Place Market, a Filipino counter is wallpapered with handwritten signs pinned up by clothespins, each one warning you to behave. They seem gruff at first and get funnier the longer you read. Oriental Mart backs up the attitude with the best lunch in the market and some of the city's finest Filipino cooking. You can get in before work and won't cost much.

entries.pullQuote: Always add fried onions, and go for the whiz if your shirt can handle it.
entries.blurb: Easy to miss and easy to trip into, Calozzi's Cheesesteaks Georgetown is a tiny roadside shack that handles any Philly craving. The beef is shaved paper thin and piled so high you'll lose some before it reaches your mouth, and while it can run a little dry, the flavor is excellent. It's an inexpensive lunch, too.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap Capitol Hill sandwich counter that's easy to slot into lunch.
entries.blurb: Inexpensive sandwiches are the whole business at Cheese Room Seattle, a Capitol Hill counter.

title: Best Brunch
dek: Late breakfast that is still worth the wait you chose.
intro:
Late breakfast that is still worth the wait you chose. Lady Jaye and Seattle Biscuit Company taste better before the day gets ambitious.

Go early. Butter, salt, and a short line beat a pretty case in the afternoon.

entries.pullQuote: Bring your meat-loving friends and don't mention that everything here is vegetarian.
entries.blurb: Take your carnivore friends to Cafe Flora and maybe skip the part where you mention it's meat-free. Smoked mozzarella pizza and mushroom risotto make a real argument for meatless cooking, and the airy greenhouse feel of the room helps too. The door opens before nine, so brunch is fair game.

entries.pullQuote: Come for weekend brunch, when the room is loud and the bread is crusty.
entries.blurb: Café Campagne has been cooking French comfort food in Post Alley for more than forty years, and the dining room still channels a Paris bistro with old posters and lamps made from wine bottles. Dinner is mellow and the steak frites are great, but brunch is when this place comes alive. Market crowds spill in to share fluffy egg dishes and good bread over upbeat music, and the check lands in special-occasion range.

entries.pullQuote: Go hungry and order a gravy-smothered biscuit sandwich with plenty of hot sauce.
entries.blurb: Biscuit Bitch serves hefty breakfast biscuits stacked with fillings, and the whole menu leans into its trailer-park-to-table joke. Try The Canadian Bitch, built on banana and maple peanut butter, or the Bitchwich loaded with sausage, egg, cheese, and gravy plus hot sauce.

entries.pullQuote: Order the purple ube pancakes and settle into a booth.
entries.blurb: Seattle mourned hard when Ludi's Restaurant closed in 2019, and the reopening a few years later felt like a homecoming. The Filipino diner now sits a couple of blocks from its old Downtown home, with the same family running the griddle and breakfast served all day. Grab a booth and get the ube pancakes, still as bright purple as ever.

entries.pullQuote: Open since 1929, and still pouring when Belltown has gone home.
entries.blurb: The 5 Point Cafe faces the five-way at Tilikum Place, and the doors have been open since 1929. It is the oldest bar in Belltown and also a cafe that can serve breakfast as a nightcap. The city already filed it under dive: a long counter, regulars who do not surrender a stool, and no interest in a redesign. Eat something that can survive a second beer. Then stay later than the plan you walked in with.

entries.pullQuote: Lower Queen Anne karaoke, priced like a dive, and open until 2.
entries.blurb: Ozzie's is a Lower Queen Anne dive with karaoke and an American kitchen, and the lights stay on until 2. Prices sit at the cheap end on purpose. Pick a song you can finish, stand where people will clap, and skip the night if nobody in the group will sing. A plainer pub can sell you a beer anywhere on Queen Anne. This room only earns the walk once the microphone is switched on.

entries.pullQuote: Start with the crispy pork balls and a pimento cheese cream puff.
entries.blurb: Lady Jaye takes West Seattle barbecue in unexpected directions, from panko-fried pulled pork balls to sandwiches piled with house bologna. Pastrami is made from pork collar, sausage goes into a creole dirty rice, and pimento cheese gets piped into cream puffs. Even the cocktails get creative with things like pumpkin seed orgeat. It's open late and works for brunch or a dinner with parents.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Gus, with fried chicken, pickles, an egg, and sausage gravy.
entries.blurb: The Fremont room feels like a boxcar diner shrunk down by a tiny-house builder, and Seattle Biscuit Company serves breakfast all day. Biscuits anchor everything, and they are excellent, whether in a sandwich like the peanut butter, apple, and jam Lunch Pail or smothered in classic gravy. Very hungry groups can tackle a huge platter of biscuits and eggs.

entries.pullQuote: Book ahead for the potato waffle benedict, and let someone else order the dutch baby.
entries.blurb: Puffy, sugar-dusted dutch babies made Tilikum Place Café a Belltown brunch fixture, but the supporting cast is the real draw. Think thick-cut bacon, smoked salmon benedict on potato waffles, and bubbling egg skillets layered with gruyere. The small room fills as soon as the doors open, so reserve a table.

entries.pullQuote: An early Capitol Hill breakfast here makes an easy win with visiting parents.
entries.blurb: Opening early for breakfast and brunch, Harry’s Fine Foods serves New American cooking that suits a meal with the folks.

entries.pullQuote: Go on a weekday morning and claim a swivel stool at the counter.
entries.blurb: Every neighborhood deserves a diner as cheerful as Geraldine's Counter, where the coffee refills never stop coming. Take a window seat, soak up the Rainier Avenue light, and work through crisp french toast and thick-cut bacon. Weekend waits run long, so a quieter weekday is the smarter play.

entries.pullQuote: The Fairfax on a warm brioche bun fixes almost any rough morning.
entries.blurb: The LA egg sandwich chain Eggslut landed on Capitol Hill, and the Fairfax, with soft scrambled eggs, chives, cheddar, and sriracha mayo on a brioche bun, is the order regulars make. Doors open early, and the bill stays gentle enough for a weekday treat.

entries.pullQuote: Order the breakfast burrito and plan to skip lunch entirely.
entries.blurb: Set in a converted Madrona house, Hi Spot Cafe still feels warm and homey, with tables spread across the upstairs rooms. The pancakes and scrambles are solid, but the hulking breakfast burrito with black beans, eggs, and vegetables is the order. It arrives with potatoes, tomatillo salsa, and sour cream you should spread over every bite.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the kids for the jukeboxes and order a breakfast pile.
entries.blurb: Sitting under the West Seattle Bridge, Luna Park Cafe is a longtime greasy spoon packed with kitsch, from vintage lunch boxes to a giant guitar and a creepy clown game. Families fill the booths on weekends, with jukeboxes at the tables to keep kids busy. The food is plainer than the decor, but the breakfast piles are a satisfying bet.

entries.pullQuote: Order the BEC on a poppy roll, then grab a pastry for later.
entries.blurb: Tucked into a house in north Capitol Hill, Volunteer Park Cafe & Pantry would be worth a visit for pastries alone, like tahini caramel bars and buckwheat chocolate chunk cookies. The breakfast sandwich is the real star, with thin folded eggs, barely crisp bacon, and melty American cheese on a toasted house poppy seed roll. Laptops aren't allowed on weekends.

entries.pullQuote: Order the chicken and waffles with Hennessy butter and a spiked fruit punch.
entries.blurb: Fat's Chicken & Waffles is where you go when the laundry can wait but the craving can't. The waffles are thin and airy with a pat of cognac butter, and the fried chicken holds its crunch even after the drive home. Eat in the laid-back Central District dining room, sweatpants welcome, with a sweet tea or boozy punch.

entries.pullQuote: Order the BBQ shrimp with grits and bring the whole birthday crew.
entries.blurb: Stick with Creole standbys at Toulouse Petit, like barbecue shrimp over grits or a bowl of seafood gumbo, and you'll leave happy. The antique-feeling Lower Queen Anne dining room hums with energy, which makes it great for birthdays and anniversaries. Brunch starts early, happy hour is popular.

entries.pullQuote: Brave the weekend line, because these hash browns justify every minute of it.
entries.blurb: Glo’s moved off its old Olive Way corner but kept the neon, the stone walls, and the mid-century charm. The wait still stretches past an hour on weekends, and it still pays off. Expect hash browns with a shattering golden crust, scallion and garlic scrambles, and a tangy homemade corned beef hash.

entries.pullQuote: An easy Market brunch stop that's open before most shops roll up their gates.
entries.blurb: Breakfast and brunch start early at Bacco Cafe, a morning stop inside the arcade.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the whole brunch crew, picky eaters and toddlers included, and nobody leaves unhappy.
entries.blurb: When a weekend brunch involves ten people with ten opinions, Portage Bay Cafe is the safe call. The menu is enormous, the ingredients lean local, and pancakes or french toast come with access to a toppings bar piled with fruit and whipped cream. You can even skip the plate entirely and just graze the bar.

entries.pullQuote: Linger over a slow lunch of roast chicken, charcuterie, and frites.
entries.blurb: Steps from the Pike Place frenzy, Le Pichet is a calm French bistro escape. It suits a long lunch, a solo dinner, or any moment the market crowds start wearing you down. Settle in and order cured pork, roast chicken, and a pile of fries.

entries.pullQuote: Order the soft herby scrambled eggs and a latte, then linger awhile.
entries.blurb: Equal parts French bistro, espresso counter, and old-fashioned grocery, Oddfellows Café and Bar leans hard into exposed brick and Capitol Hill cool. Come early for coffee and soft scrambled eggs with cheese and herbs, or show up later for cocktails on the patio or a relaxed dinner date. There are no reservations, and weekend brunch is busier than dinner, so have a backup in mind.

entries.pullQuote: A warm crumpet with ricotta and pesto beats every other quick breakfast at the market.
entries.blurb: Breakfast options at Pike Place Market are thin, which makes The Crumpet Shop so useful. The crumpets are springy and crisp, and their little holes trap toppings like pesto with ricotta or raspberry preserves. Be there while the crumpets are still warm and hardly anything is spent.

entries.pullQuote: Gluten-free diners should head straight for the pancakes with cinnamon butter.
entries.blurb: If gluten is your nemesis, Bounty Kitchen belongs on your brunch shortlist. The bright all-day cafe on Queen Anne makes excellent gluten-free pancakes topped with fruit compote and cinnamon butter, plus egg and vegetable hashes. Wheat-friendly tables can go for the braised beef bowl or avocado toast, and expect a short wait during the weekend rush.

title: Happy Hour
dek: After-work bars and kitchens, when one round should turn into dinner.
intro:
After-work bars and kitchens, when one round should turn into dinner. Dead Line and Il Terrazzo Carmine are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Pioneer Square, Fremont, Downtown without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Pioneer Square, Fremont, Downtown will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Marrow-rich ossobuco and white-jacketed waiters at Pioneer Square's Italian standby since 1984.
entries.blurb: Order the ossobuco, a thick veal shank over buttered fettuccine, after a plate from the antipasto bar. Carmine Smeraldo opened it in 1984.

entries.pullQuote: The late pour is the excuse, and the salmon nigiri is why anyone stays.
entries.blurb: Before Momiji, there was Umi Sake House, and the first one is still the pick. Ask for the back dining room, which feels like a bamboo garden turned lounge, and order a nigiri sampler plus rolls with seared snow crab or spicy yellowtail. Big groups can usually book even the night before, and the happy hour and late kitchen help.

entries.pullQuote: Order a classic cocktail and the lamb pastitsio, then share a booth.
entries.blurb: Zig Zag Café is known for cocktails, but skipping the Greek food here would be a mistake. Go for the lamb pastitsio, marinated chicken kebabs with a side of tzatziki, and a sesame-rich hummus. Booths force you onto the same side. It stays open late, and happy hour is a classic.

entries.pullQuote: Goat cheese and lavender fondue and a Palace Burger Royale at Tom Douglas's late bar.
entries.blurb: Order the goat cheese-lavender fondue with apples and grilled focaccia, then the Palace Burger Royale. Grab a stool at the big bar in Belltown.

entries.pullQuote: Long communal tables and liters of German beer make group nights easy.
entries.blurb: Near Seattle Center, Queen Anne Beerhall is a roomy German-style beer hall with shared tables and plenty of space for a crowd. That early drink deal is a solid deal, and the bar keeps pouring well past eleven, which helps after a game or concert next door.

entries.pullQuote: Come for pico-topped rolls and sukiyaki tacos when you want a flashy dinner.
entries.blurb: Japonessa Sushi Cocina mixes sushi with Latin flavors, so rolls get salsa and tortillas get filled with beef sukiyaki. It's loud, touristy, and busy even midweek, but the fish is reliably good. Happy hour and a late kitchen make it an easy Downtown call.

entries.pullQuote: Butternut squash enchiladas and margaritas at the corner of Terry and Harrison.
entries.blurb: Order the butternut squash enchiladas with apricot-chocolate mole rojo, or the brisket tacos on fresh corn tortillas. Weekend brunch runs 10 to 2.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a deck table at happy hour and order a cup of chowder.
entries.blurb: Lake Union views and a packed deck pull a crowd into Duke's Seafood South Lake Union, along with the creamy clam chowder the local chain built its name on. The pre-dinner window is a solid deal.

entries.pullQuote: Lobster mac and cheese beside a 30-foot tower of wine near Benaroya Hall.
entries.blurb: Order the Maine lobster mac and cheese and a glass from the long list. The wine tower anchors the room; happy hour runs weekdays 2 to 5.

entries.pullQuote: Come at happy hour, when the chips, olives, and nuts arrive free with drinks.
entries.blurb: Dead Line is small, dark, and polished, with shelves of bottles so tall the bartenders need a rolling ladder. Beyond the serious cocktails, the kitchen turns out South American small plates like brisket arepas and squash al pastor tacos. The pre-dinner window is a steal, and the bar pours past eleven.

entries.pullQuote: Order the belly dip with house chips first, then a crab roll.
entries.blurb: Local Tide makes a case for Seattle seafood beyond salmon and chowder, though it nails those too. At this Fremont counter, the smoked belly dip with thin, house-seasoned chips is a must. Sandwiches are the main event, from the weekend crab roll with lemon mayo and chives to a dover sole take on the Filet-O-Fish. Shrimp toast with pork fat and a happy hour make it easy to come back.

entries.pullQuote: Take a bar stool, order a dirty martini, and work through a dozen oysters.
entries.blurb: Inside the Fairmont Olympic, SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR is an old-school room that smells faintly of brine and polished leather. Happy hour knocks the price of local raw oysters way down, and the baked ones topped with toasted brioche and lemony herb butter deserve a spot in your order. The space was a haberdashery in the early twentieth century, and it still has that buttoned-up charm.

entries.pullQuote: Order the doughnuts with mascarpone for the table and break the ice.
entries.blurb: Lola brings Greek cooking to Belltown in a room that lands right between casual and upscale, which makes it ideal for having a new partner meet your parents. Brunch calls for the seasonal scramble, and dinner calls for the lamb burger. Then get the cinnamon doughnuts, which come with vanilla bean mascarpone and a fruit compote, and eat one in a single bite.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a seat on the roof deck and make happy hour a seafood dinner.
entries.blurb: Fremont's RockCreek Seafood & Spirits is a lively seafood house with a long menu of fish and shellfish and a solid cocktail list. Happy hour draws a crowd, and when the weather cooperates, the rooftop is where you want to be.

entries.pullQuote: Brisket pho and a gin cocktail in a dark, moody room is the move.
entries.blurb: Ba Bar pulls off a very particular mood, bowls of brisket phở and gin drinks under low light with jazz playing. The towering bar is the first thing you see, tall enough to need a ladder and backed by a giant vintage Vietnamese rock album poster. It feels like a candlelit back alley with nice furniture, and it's open late with a happy hour worth catching.

entries.pullQuote: Reserve the big round table, order the brûléed mac and cheese, and share.
entries.blurb: Dinner at Shaker + Spear feels a bit like eating in a very nice home goods showroom, in the best way. The seafood is strong, the staff is sharp and warm, and one round table seats eight if you're bringing a group. Order the prawns in Old Bay butter, the parmesan truffle fries, the charred sprouts, and that torched mac and cheese, then move next door to Pennyroyal for cocktails.

entries.pullQuote: Come at sunset, when the view over Elliott Bay does most of the work.
entries.blurb: Inside the Edgewater Hotel on the waterfront, Six Seven Restaurant is all about the scenery, with big windows and a deck right over the water. The Northwest menu leans on seafood, and happy hour is the low-commitment way to soak it all in.

entries.pullQuote: Order the BBQ shrimp with grits and bring the whole birthday crew.
entries.blurb: Stick with Creole standbys at Toulouse Petit, like barbecue shrimp over grits or a bowl of seafood gumbo, and you'll leave happy. The antique-feeling Lower Queen Anne dining room hums with energy, which makes it great for birthdays and anniversaries. Brunch starts early, happy hour is popular.

entries.pullQuote: Call here when you need a last-minute birthday table for a dozen friends.
entries.blurb: The menu at Re:public dresses up comfort food, with burgers, Nashville hot chicken sandwiches, and mac and cheese loaded with prawns and pork belly. It's more about the mood than the cooking, especially in summer when the garage doors roll up. Groups can usually claim a section of the bar with little notice, the kitchen stays open late, and there's a happy hour too.

entries.pullQuote: A late Belltown sushi spot with a happy hour worth planning around.
entries.blurb: Belltown's Wasabi Sushi & Izakaya serves sushi and izakaya plates late into the night, and the discounted hour is a strong reason to stop in.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the sunny-afternoon crowds and come after dark for the lit-up lake.
entries.blurb: Nautical decor and big water views make The White Swan Public House look like a tourist trap, but it mostly sidesteps the clichés. Stick with the seafood and you'll eat well. Warm afternoons get packed, so come after sundown, when tables open up and party boats drift across Lake Union. Happy hour and big groups are both easy here.

entries.pullQuote: Bocce, a boot of lager, and bratwurst in a Capitol Hill hall.
entries.blurb: Rhein Haus is a Capitol Hill beer hall of long wooden tables, bratwurst, and bocce played hard enough to sour a friendship. Lager arrives by the liter in a glass boot. Pretzels come with beer cheese, and warm months set the slushie machines spinning. The bathroom line can outlast a sitcom episode. The crowd is young and loud, which is the recommendation. Claim a lane before the hall claims your whole night.

entries.pullQuote: Swing by after work for crab dip, cauliflower, and a round of cocktails.
entries.blurb: Before trading work clothes for sweatpants, stop into Black Bottle in Belltown for a drink. The menu runs long, covering Korean fried chicken bites, spicy cauliflower, and a cheesy Dungeness crab dip, so you can mix it up on every visit. There's a happy hour.

entries.pullQuote: Gather a big group, order pints of Space Dust, and settle in.
entries.blurb: Big tables, a long tap list, and Space Dust IPA at the source make Elysian Brewing - Capitol Hill a simple yes for groups. Happy hour helps, and the pub keeps pouring late.

entries.pullQuote: Settle into a dark corner and order something stirred, strong, and classic.
entries.blurb: A dark, grown-up Belltown bar, Rob Roy takes cocktails seriously without getting precious about them. Happy hour is the smart way in, and the bartenders are as comfortable with the classics as with their own inventions.

entries.pullQuote: Pineapple on the fried fish, a painkiller, and a booth big enough for Uno.
entries.blurb: Bait Shop cannot pick between a nautical dive and a tiki shack, so the Capitol Hill room does both. Pineapple or bacon can land on the fried fish, and the fries have their own local following. Frozen drinks change by the day. Learn the painkiller by name: rum, pineapple, coconut, orange, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Take a big booth, deal a hand of Uno, and leave the amaro lecture for a different door on the hill.

entries.pullQuote: Sip an amaro at the long wooden bar while waiting for a table next door.
entries.blurb: Barnacle pours beside Ballard's famous oyster bar, and it might be the cooler room. One long wood counter is the whole floor plan, a bowl of Lay's lands at your elbow, and the bartenders make drinks that embarrass a home setup. Oysters, cured meats, and cheese suit a promising date, and the early drink window is worth using.

entries.pullQuote: Order raw oysters by the dozen and grab the wall tables if you brought a date.
entries.blurb: Taylor Shellfish Farms has been growing oysters in Washington for well over a century, and this Pioneer Square bar puts that harvest on ice. Branch out with Dungeness crab or Manila clams once the first round is gone. Couples should claim the tables along the wall, and the bar is there when you would rather face the shells than each other. Happy hour makes a second round easier to justify.

entries.pullQuote: Come before sunset, sit at the marble bar, and order oysters by the dozen.
entries.blurb: The Walrus and The Carpenter draws an oyster line in Ballard even though the bay is nowhere in sight. The room feels like a farmhouse that traded livestock for shellfish, and it shines in late afternoon when sunlight bounces off the mirrors. Happy hour helps, and a date here rarely goes wrong.

title: Best Sandwiches
dek: Bread, filling, and the ones you eat before they steam themselves.
intro:
Bread, filling, and the ones you eat before they steam themselves. Fortuna Bottega and Louie's Deli are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Greenwood, Pioneer Square, Denny Triangle without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Greenwood, Pioneer Square, Denny Triangle will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.
entries.blurb: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.

entries.pullQuote: Philly cheesesteak or pastrami are both hits here, and it might be the best cheesesteak in the city.
entries.blurb: Philly cheesesteak or pastrami are both hits here, and it might be the best cheesesteak in the city.

entries.pullQuote: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.
entries.blurb: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.

entries.pullQuote: Bacon, egg and cheese on a poppy seed bagel.
entries.blurb: The Good Shape Pizza team turned its attention to sandwiches at Louie's Deli, a royal blue counter in Pioneer Square. Sesame hoagie rolls are crunchy and chewy, bacon is chopped into small bits, and cold cuts are shaved impossibly thin. The bacon, egg and cheese is on a poppy seed bagel. There's an arcade room next door for pinball after lunch.

entries.pullQuote: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.
entries.blurb: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.

entries.pullQuote: Come in with friends or solo, best turkey sandwich around.
entries.blurb: Come in with friends or solo, best turkey sandwich around.

entries.pullQuote: Different from the traditional bánh mì, but that side of beef bone marrow broth makes it uniquely amazing and a must.
entries.blurb: Different from the traditional bánh mì, but that side of beef bone marrow broth makes it uniquely amazing and a must.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Thanksgiving turkey sandwich and add tater tots for dunking.
entries.blurb: Valhalla Sandwiches in Greenwood manages to go big without getting sloppy. The sandwiches come on sturdy telera rolls with fillings like blackened shrimp and chorizo, chicken with sweet-hot mustard and slaw, or turkey with stuffing, cranberry, and rosemary aioli. Tater tots with chipotle mayo are a must, and the whole thing is inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: Honestly, everything is good here, but my favorite is the TBR (turkey, bacon, ranch). Pro tip: get the spuds on the side.
entries.blurb: Honestly, everything is good here, but my favorite is the TBR (turkey, bacon, ranch). Pro tip: get the spuds on the side.

entries.pullQuote: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.
entries.blurb: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap toasted subs that hit hardest when it's late and you're starving.
entries.blurb: A stoner-themed chain counter near the university, Cheba Hut Toasted Subs keeps the oven running late and the prices low.

entries.pullQuote: Griddled corned beef with mint and pickled cabbage, from a Momofuku alum.
entries.blurb: Order the Mean: thick griddled corned beef, house yellow mustard, pickled red cabbage and fresh mint on a challah bun. It comes with the salt-and-pepper potato skins.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap Italian sandwiches in Greenwood, no reservation needed, just show up hungry.
entries.blurb: Fortuna Bottega makes inexpensive Italian sandwiches at a walk-up Greenwood counter.

entries.pullQuote: The corned beef reuben here is the benchmark for every deli in town.
entries.blurb: Look for the huge corned beef sign over the Denny Triangle and you've found Market House Meats. The shop has fed office workers and early construction crews since the forties, and the griddle is always sizzling. That tender, salty corned beef goes into a reuben you'll measure every other one against. It's inexpensive, quick, and open early.

entries.pullQuote: Get the Italian sub, add a breakfast sandwich, and bring patience.
entries.blurb: The owners once ran Lyon's Grocery in Queen Anne, and that pedigree shows in every sandwich at Otherside Market & Deli in Eastlake. The Italian sub piles on ham with pepperoncini and a hit of red wine vinegar, while breakfast sandwiches arrive gooey on Backyard bagels. Even a plain turkey and cheese on wheat is great here.

entries.pullQuote: After a Green Lake loop, bring the dog and order jerk chicken.
entries.blurb: Bongos Cafe lives in a brightly painted old gas station by the lake, and the beachy patio always feels like a party. The jerk chicken is excellent, the Caribbean sandwiches stand up to the best around, and the fried yucca balls come filled with molten cheese. Wash it all down with a coconut-heavy piña, and brace yourself for the spicy shrimp.

entries.pullQuote: Order the chicken caesar wrap, then come back another day for the reuben.
entries.blurb: Take 5 Urban Market has the Moon Pies and fruit sodas of a proper corner store, plus a short sandwich menu that deserves real attention. The reuben swaps kraut for creamy slaw and gets a crisp layer of griddled swiss, and the sriracha chicken melt brings plenty of avocado and actual heat. Still, the one you will crave is the chicken caesar, packed with bacon, tomato, and crouton bits.

entries.pullQuote: The Fairfax on a warm brioche bun fixes almost any rough morning.
entries.blurb: The LA egg sandwich chain Eggslut landed on Capitol Hill, and the Fairfax, with soft scrambled eggs, chives, cheddar, and sriracha mayo on a brioche bun, is the order regulars make. Doors open early, and the bill stays gentle enough for a weekday treat.

entries.pullQuote: The grilled pork bánh mì here is still a cheap lunch miracle.
entries.blurb: Prices creep up everywhere, but Saigon Viet Nam Deli in the International District still sells a bánh mì that barely dents your wallet. The grilled pork version comes on crackly fresh bread with a generous swipe of bơ and plenty of coarse black pepper. It tastes the same every time, which is the highest compliment.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Caribbean Roast and grab extra napkins, you will need them.
entries.blurb: Seattle's most famous sandwich might be the Caribbean Roast at Paseo, a pile of marinated roast pork and caramelized onions on a toasted baguette. It's gloriously messy, so eat it right away in Fremont rather than letting it sit.

entries.pullQuote: Always add fried onions, and go for the whiz if your shirt can handle it.
entries.blurb: Easy to miss and easy to trip into, Calozzi's Cheesesteaks Georgetown is a tiny roadside shack that handles any Philly craving. The beef is shaved paper thin and piled so high you'll lose some before it reaches your mouth, and while it can run a little dry, the flavor is excellent. It's an inexpensive lunch, too.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap Capitol Hill sandwich counter that's easy to slot into lunch.
entries.blurb: Inexpensive sandwiches are the whole business at Cheese Room Seattle, a Capitol Hill counter.

entries.pullQuote: Get the pastrami on rye and a pickle, and you're set until dinner.
entries.blurb: East Coast Jewish deli energy comes to Capitol Hill at Dingfelder's Delicatessen, where piled-high pastrami sandwiches carry the meal. Morning service starts first and keeps the prices friendly.

entries.pullQuote: Late-night sandwich cravings on Capitol Hill have a reliable answer right here.
entries.blurb: Cheap sandwiches and a kitchen that runs late make Honeyhole Sandwiches a Capitol Hill standby.

entries.pullQuote: Split the Italian with a friend, or don't, and grab a bag of chips.
entries.blurb: Proper East Coast-style subs are rare in Seattle, which makes Royal Grinders in Fremont a real asset. The Italian is what you should request, stacked with pepperoni, salami, ham, provolone, swiss, and chopped pepperoncini on bread that's crisp outside and soft within, plus a ranch spread you'll want to take home. Every sandwich here is massive, so sharing is reasonable.

title: Best Burgers
dek: Patties from drive-in to sit-down.
intro:
Patties from drive-in to sit-down. Uneeda Burger and Ox Burger are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Fremont, Central District, Phinney Ridge without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Fremont, Central District, Phinney Ridge will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: The bacon-beef burger and herby shoestring fries are worth earning with a hike.
entries.blurb: Patties topped with special sauce, sharp aged cheddar, sweet onions, and thick-cut pickles are the headliners at Big Max Burger Co. The Nashville-style hot chicken sandwich, glazed with smoky chili and served with plenty of ranch, is just as good. Round things out with a milkshake, kettle corn brussels sprouts, or puffy chicken nuggets and sweet and sour sauce.

entries.pullQuote: A no-fuss Fremont counter for a cheap burger without a reservation.
entries.blurb: Walk in, order at the counter, and Uneeda Burger will hand you an inexpensive burger in Fremont.

entries.pullQuote: Eat a double cheeseburger and a root beer float in the car.
entries.blurb: For a double cheeseburger with fries and a shake on pocket change, Pick-Quick Drive In has you covered. The burgers beat Dick's handily, and you get to sit down while you eat them. Load your friends into the car and get everyone root beer floats made with real soft serve.

entries.pullQuote: A Deluxe, fries, and a chocolate shake is a Seattle rite of passage.
entries.blurb: Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap Central District burger fix you can grab at the counter.
entries.blurb: Inexpensive burgers from a casual counter make Ox Burger an easy Central District stop.

entries.pullQuote: Get onion rings to dunk in fry sauce, plus a mint truffle shake.
entries.blurb: Nobody comes to Red Mill Burgers for gourmet toppings or atmosphere. You come for a charbroiled diner-style patty, cornmeal-crusted onion rings dunked in fry sauce, and a thick shake in flavors like s'mores. Grab a spot at one of the bright red picnic tables, ideally after a hike or a slow afternoon around Phinney Ridge.

title: Italian & Pasta
dek: Pasta shops and Italian dining rooms, not another pizza list.
intro:
Pasta shops and Italian dining rooms, not another pizza list. il nido and Lioness are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through West Seattle, Phinney Ridge, Pike Place Market without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. West Seattle, Phinney Ridge, Pike Place Market will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Marrow-rich ossobuco and white-jacketed waiters at Pioneer Square's Italian standby since 1984.
entries.blurb: Order the ossobuco, a thick veal shank over buttered fettuccine, after a plate from the antipasto bar. Carmine Smeraldo opened it in 1984.

entries.pullQuote: Go for the lasagna and the cabaret, and fight for a seat on the deck.
entries.blurb: Behind an unmarked pink door in Post Alley, The Pink Door has paired Italian-American comfort food with trapeze acts and cabaret for decades. The summer deck looks out over Elliott Bay, and lasagna is the order. It works for a date, a visiting friend, or a late dinner near Pike Place Market.

entries.pullQuote: Cioppino in a candlelit grotto under Pike Place.
entries.blurb: Order the cioppino or the rigatoni Bolognese in this candlelit room down a cobblestone alley under the market, open for more than 50 years.

entries.pullQuote: Rigatoni Bolognese under the soaring rotunda windows downtown.
entries.blurb: Order the rigatoni Bolognese, a Carmine family classic, or the newer osso buco ravioli. It's the Smeraldo family's downtown room, after Il Terrazzo.

entries.pullQuote: Mushroom fettuccine beside the Belltown courtyard fountain, since 1994.
entries.blurb: Order the fettuccine ai funghi, the best seller, or the squid-ink linguine with salmon. There's been a table by the courtyard fountain since 1994.

entries.pullQuote: Get the pomodoro with burrata and leave space for the ricotta crostata.
entries.blurb: Inside Pike Place Market, Pasta Casalinga turns out handmade bowls that would hold their own in Italy. The rotating menu pulls from ocean, garden, and farm, think rigatoni with lamb and juniper ragu or spaghettoni tossed in kale pesto. The best bowl is the simplest one, pomodoro topped with a cool spoonful of burrata. If the ricotta chocolate crostata is on, order it, and bring your parents.

entries.pullQuote: Bring a date to Wallingford for an Italian dinner that feels relaxed.
entries.blurb: Couples looking for an Italian date night in Wallingford can count on Cantinetta.

entries.pullQuote: Rigatoni Bolognese and bucatini carbonara with a skyline-to-Olympics view in Mount Baker.
entries.blurb: Order the rigatoni Bolognese or the bucatini carbonara, and ask for a table facing the view. Clear evenings reach the Olympics.

entries.pullQuote: Bucatini and bone-marrow meatballs at Two Union Square.
entries.blurb: Get the bucatini with beef-and-ricotta meatballs in a marrow-enriched tomato sauce. The pasta is made fresh daily, and the pizza dough proofs for three days.

entries.pullQuote: Lobster risotto and truffle-sausage gnocchi at a candlelit Westlake Italian open until 11.
entries.blurb: Order the lobster tail risotto with shrimp bisque, or the house gnocchi with black truffle and sausage. Dinner runs nightly from 3 to 11.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a bar seat solo and twirl through a plate of amatriciana.
entries.blurb: Darkalino's took over the old London Plane space in Pioneer Square, keeping the towering columns, huge windows, and all that brick. The all-day Italian menu is casual, and the pasta all'amatriciana is the thing to get. Romance isn't really the vibe, so come alone or bring a crew of friends while wedding-reception hits play overhead.

entries.pullQuote: An easy U District pick for Italian dinner and a pizza to share.
entries.blurb: Mamma Melina Ristorante + Pizzeria serves Italian plates and pizza to a U District crowd.

entries.pullQuote: Book the Spheres room when a Roman pizza night should feel like a splurge.
entries.blurb: Renee Erickson's Willmott's Ghost sits inside the Amazon Spheres, a blush-pink room serving Roman-inspired Italian food. Order the Roman-style pizza and pastas, and plan on a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: This is where West Seattle goes for anniversaries and unfussy pasta nights alike.
entries.blurb: Alki may feel like a summer-only scene, but il nido gives West Seattle a reason to go out all year. The Italian cooking is consistent enough that even a plain bowl of noodles lands, and the staff handles off-menu requests without blinking. It sits inside a historic homestead, which makes the setting feel special without getting stuffy.

entries.pullQuote: Stand at the marble bar with a bergamot spritz and a few snacks.
entries.blurb: Phinney Ridge's Lioness turns Italian aperitivo hour into an actual event. The narrow room glows with tea lights and a pair of chandeliers, and the soundtrack runs as fast as the date night chatter. Folks crowd the standing marble counter over bergamot spritzes, zero-proof garibaldis, and spotless martinis.

entries.pullQuote: Grab two seats at the long bar for an easy, early-stage date.
entries.blurb: Walking up to Artusi, you catch the smell of grilled bread and olive oil drifting from the kitchen, and the night only gets better inside. This smaller sibling to Spinasse is mostly one big L-shaped counter, and that's where you want to be for sharp cocktails and Italian snacks. It suits a newer date or any night when you want great food in lighter portions.

entries.pullQuote: Order every pasta you can justify, starting with the buttery tajarin.
entries.blurb: For a splurge Italian dinner in Seattle, Spinasse sets the bar, with handmade Piedmontese pasta and service that runs like clockwork. The Capitol Hill dining room mixes reclaimed wood with a sleek marble bar and an open kitchen where you can watch the noodles being made. Expect a special-occasion check, and know the kitchen keeps going late.

entries.pullQuote: A dependable Belltown Italian dining room for a relaxed weeknight dinner.
entries.blurb: Anyone in Belltown looking for a sit-down Italian meal can head to Assaggio Ristorante.

entries.pullQuote: Bring a date here when you need dinner to go exactly as planned.
entries.blurb: Some restaurants just know what you need, and San Fermo in Ballard is reliable in exactly that way. Set in a pair of old houses, the room feels warm and lived-in, and the pasta gives you a reason to come back. It's the Italian spot you book when there's no room for a dud evening.

entries.pullQuote: Book the garden patio on a warm night and order a bottle of red.
entries.blurb: Eastlake's Serafina has been a romantic Italian standby for decades, with a warm, rustic room and a leafy back patio. It's an easy call for an anniversary or a long dinner over pasta and wine.

entries.pullQuote: Hide out here with a bowl of pasta and a good bottle of wine.
entries.blurb: Opened by the people behind Le Messe, Vendemmia is a quiet Madrona escape built around pasta and wine. Pick a bottle, then choose between spaghetti with tomato and chili or taleggio-filled agnolotti. Expect a special-occasion bill, and treat it as a reliable date night.

entries.pullQuote: Late Italian in Belltown for when a bar menu just won't do.
entries.blurb: Cotto Belltown serves Italian food and keeps the kitchen going late, which counts for a lot around here.

entries.pullQuote: Book it for date night when everyone at the table is craving Italian.
entries.blurb: Cornelly makes a strong case for an Italian dinner date on Capitol Hill.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the pricey entrees and order the margherita with a pasta on the side.
entries.blurb: Blue neon under the bar and champagne bottles as decor make Cinque Terre Ristorante feel a bit like a hotel lobby. Ignore that, because the Neapolitan pies are the real deal, with a charred, crackly crust and a balanced layer of San Marzano and mozzarella. Round things out with casarecce tossed with pesto and ricotta, or boar sugo over rigatoni, and leave the main courses alone.

entries.pullQuote: Save this Capitol Hill tasting menu for an anniversary or a milestone date.
entries.blurb: Big nights on Capitol Hill often end up at Altura, where a multi-course Italian tasting menu leans on Northwest ingredients. The check is firmly in special-occasion territory, so bring it out for a celebration that deserves the fuss.

entries.pullQuote: A dependable downtown Italian dining room for pasta before a night out.
entries.blurb: Downtown's Tulio has been serving Italian food out of the Hotel Vintage for decades, and pasta is the draw.

entries.pullQuote: A Capitol Hill Italian option for an easygoing weeknight bowl of something comforting.
entries.blurb: Due' Cucina Italiana cooks Italian food on Capitol Hill for neighborhood dinners.

entries.pullQuote: Save this Lower Queen Anne Italian spot for your next date night.
entries.blurb: For an Italian date night by Seattle Center, Messina is a strong call.

entries.pullQuote: A Magnolia Italian dinner that saves you the drive across town.
entries.blurb: Mondello Italian Restaurant gives Magnolia a neighborhood Italian dinner option close to home.

entries.pullQuote: Neapolitan pies with real char and crispness make this a Beacon Hill classic.
entries.blurb: A big, leisurely dinner at Bar Del Corso ranks among the most reliably happy nights in Seattle. Neapolitan pizza and small plates keep this Beacon Hill Italian spot packed most evenings. The crust is charred with a light crispness all the way through, a welcome contrast to the floppier pies around town.

entries.pullQuote: Settle into the snug room and order a couple of handmade pastas.
entries.blurb: Named after a wartime cookbook, How to Cook a Wolf turns out fresh pasta and Italian small plates in an intimate Queen Anne room. The kitchen runs late, so Queen Anne can still get pasta after the first plan falls through.

title: Seafood & Oysters
dek: Fish, oysters, and chowder, because the city is made of water.
intro:
Fish, oysters, and chowder, because the city is made of water. Driftwood and Local Tide are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through West Seattle, Fremont, Downtown without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. West Seattle, Fremont, Downtown will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: New England clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl, with oyster crackers, in Post Alley.
entries.blurb: Get the clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl and add oyster crackers. Skip the smoked salmon chowder.

entries.pullQuote: Order the cod and the Greek-spiced fried oysters, and eat by the beach.
entries.blurb: Few things say West Seattle like Sunfish, an Alki fish and chips counter that goes dark for most of winter and flips its neon sign back on around February. Squeeze lemon over battered cod that flakes apart and meaty oysters fried with Greek spices for a sunny, casual lunch near the sand.

entries.pullQuote: Panko-crusted cod and Cajun fried shrimp at a Fremont dive since 1981.
entries.blurb: Order the fish and chips: thin Pacific cod in a peppery, garlicky panko crust. Add the Cajun fried shrimp and eat on the deck; the pub is 21 and over.

entries.pullQuote: Get the blackened salmon sandwich with rosemary mayo and a cup of chowder.
entries.blurb: Squeezing through Pike Place crowds sounds like a bad lunch plan, but Market Grill makes it pay off. The counter sits right in the middle of the action, where the cooks sear a blackened salmon sandwich slicked in rosemary mayo. Add the herby clam chowder on the side. Solo diners can usually snag a stool, while groups should take it to go.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a deck table at happy hour and order a cup of chowder.
entries.blurb: Lake Union views and a packed deck pull a crowd into Duke's Seafood South Lake Union, along with the creamy clam chowder the local chain built its name on. The pre-dinner window is a solid deal.

entries.pullQuote: Fine for a patio break with visitors, but skip the pricey crab.
entries.blurb: Up at the north end of Pike Place, Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder caters to tourists with a menu that comes and goes in quality. The fried fish is fine, and the bacon-y clam chowder with its Goldfish-style crackers is the strongest play. A breezy patio over Elliott Bay makes it a decent rest stop with guests.

entries.pullQuote: Stick with spritzes, small plates, and the excellent bread, and you'll leave happy.
entries.blurb: Pastel, polished, and very Alki, Driftwood calls for dressing up a little while keeping the sandals on. The seafood mains can get fussy with too many toppings, but the cocktails are refreshing and the smaller dishes hold up nicely. Order the table bread, which ranks with the city's best, and make it a date.

entries.pullQuote: Order the belly dip with house chips first, then a crab roll.
entries.blurb: Local Tide makes a case for Seattle seafood beyond salmon and chowder, though it nails those too. At this Fremont counter, the smoked belly dip with thin, house-seasoned chips is a must. Sandwiches are the main event, from the weekend crab roll with lemon mayo and chives to a dover sole take on the Filet-O-Fish. Shrimp toast with pork fat and a happy hour make it easy to come back.

entries.pullQuote: Take a bar stool, order a dirty martini, and work through a dozen oysters.
entries.blurb: Inside the Fairmont Olympic, SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR is an old-school room that smells faintly of brine and polished leather. Happy hour knocks the price of local raw oysters way down, and the baked ones topped with toasted brioche and lemony herb butter deserve a spot in your order. The space was a haberdashery in the early twentieth century, and it still has that buttoned-up charm.

entries.pullQuote: Pay the extra few bucks for halibut and eat it near the beach.
entries.blurb: Alki Spud Fish and Chips has been frying seafood by the beach since the thirties, and old photos and maps of West Seattle cover the walls to prove it. The halibut costs a little more and is absolutely the order, flaky and tender under a crisp, well-seasoned batter. Portions can run huge, and it all comes cheap enough when midday has to be fast or a visit with out-of-town guests.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a seat on the roof deck and make happy hour a seafood dinner.
entries.blurb: Fremont's RockCreek Seafood & Spirits is a lively seafood house with a long menu of fish and shellfish and a solid cocktail list. Happy hour draws a crowd, and when the weather cooperates, the rooftop is where you want to be.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap, early U District cafe with a seafood bent worth checking out.
entries.blurb: Seafood and cafe fare share the menu at Seafab, an inexpensive U District spot that opens early.

entries.pullQuote: Order the poke with spicy salmon and a scoop of smoky mac salad.
entries.blurb: The poke at Seattle Fish Guys in the Central District earns a spot on any short list of things that never disappoint. Each piece pulls its weight, from the soy-soaked tuna and spicy salmon to the furikake-dusted rice and smoky mac salad, and together they add up to something even better.

entries.pullQuote: Reserve the big round table, order the brûléed mac and cheese, and share.
entries.blurb: Dinner at Shaker + Spear feels a bit like eating in a very nice home goods showroom, in the best way. The seafood is strong, the staff is sharp and warm, and one round table seats eight if you're bringing a group. Order the prawns in Old Bay butter, the parmesan truffle fries, the charred sprouts, and that torched mac and cheese, then move next door to Pennyroyal for cocktails.

entries.pullQuote: Alder-smoked salmon on the Lake Union deck is the plate that matters.
entries.blurb: The Wallingford Ivar's faces Lake Union, and alder-smoked salmon justifies stopping at take a deck table. Clam chowder can sit beside it. Come for the water without making a ferry out of dinner.

entries.pullQuote: Seafood up top in Belltown, best saved for a clear evening.
entries.blurb: For seafood with rooftop seating in Belltown, MARKET at the Park is the move.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a rooftop seat on a clear day and order the seafood.
entries.blurb: Harry's Beach House brings seafood, an open-air roof deck, and morning hours to West Seattle.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the sunny-afternoon crowds and come after dark for the lit-up lake.
entries.blurb: Nautical decor and big water views make The White Swan Public House look like a tourist trap, but it mostly sidesteps the clichés. Stick with the seafood and you'll eat well. Warm afternoons get packed, so come after sundown, when tables open up and party boats drift across Lake Union. Happy hour and big groups are both easy here.

entries.pullQuote: Come for seafood and stay for the view over the water.
entries.blurb: Seafood and outdoor seating with a view pull a crowd into AQUA by El Gaucho, a polished Belltown spot.

entries.pullQuote: Pineapple on the fried fish, a painkiller, and a booth big enough for Uno.
entries.blurb: Bait Shop cannot pick between a nautical dive and a tiki shack, so the Capitol Hill room does both. Pineapple or bacon can land on the fried fish, and the fries have their own local following. Frozen drinks change by the day. Learn the painkiller by name: rum, pineapple, coconut, orange, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Take a big booth, deal a hand of Uno, and leave the amaro lecture for a different door on the hill.

entries.pullQuote: Sip an amaro at the long wooden bar while waiting for a table next door.
entries.blurb: Barnacle pours beside Ballard's famous oyster bar, and it might be the cooler room. One long wood counter is the whole floor plan, a bowl of Lay's lands at your elbow, and the bartenders make drinks that embarrass a home setup. Oysters, cured meats, and cheese suit a promising date, and the early drink window is worth using.

entries.pullQuote: Order the ahi tostada with salsa macha and a crisp saison.
entries.blurb: Running a Mexican seafood kitchen inside Fair Isle Brewing, La Marea proves brewery food can go well beyond burgers. Crunchy tostadas lead the menu, especially the one stacked with buttery ahi and fiery salsa macha. Pair it with a farmhouse saison to tame the heat.

entries.pullQuote: Order raw oysters by the dozen and grab the wall tables if you brought a date.
entries.blurb: Taylor Shellfish Farms has been growing oysters in Washington for well over a century, and this Pioneer Square bar puts that harvest on ice. Branch out with Dungeness crab or Manila clams once the first round is gone. Couples should claim the tables along the wall, and the bar is there when you would rather face the shells than each other. Happy hour makes a second round easier to justify.

entries.pullQuote: Come before sunset, sit at the marble bar, and order oysters by the dozen.
entries.blurb: The Walrus and The Carpenter draws an oyster line in Ballard even though the bay is nowhere in sight. The room feels like a farmhouse that traded livestock for shellfish, and it shines in late afternoon when sunlight bounces off the mirrors. Happy hour helps, and a date here rarely goes wrong.

title: Ramen, Pho & Noodles
dek: Bowls for gray weather: ramen, phở, and the other noodles.
intro:
Bowls for gray weather: ramen, phở, and the other noodles. Bé Mi and Kajiken are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill, Greenwood without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill, Greenwood will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Order the garlic fried chicken rice and eat lunch aboard a landlocked wooden ship.
entries.blurb: Docked in a parking lot in the International District, The Boat is a wooden ship the Phở Bắc team brought back to life in 2022. The main reason to climb aboard is the fried Cornish hen over rice, slicked with garlicky fish sauce. Think of it as a quick, unfussy lunch that doesn't require much planning.

entries.pullQuote: These loaded bánh mì prove that more toppings can absolutely mean better.
entries.blurb: Bé Mi skips the minimalist approach to bánh mì, layering on crushed peanuts, chili jam, fried shallots, and heaps of herbs. The fillings hold their own, whether it's charred, fatty pork or cold cuts with pâté. The dining room has just enough energy and makes a good escape from the Pioneer Square tour crowds.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the broth and go all in on a bowl of saucy aburasoba.
entries.blurb: Kajiken specializes in aburasoba, a brothless style of ramen where springy noodles get tossed in a rich sauce at the bottom of the bowl. The Capitol Hill shop keeps things casual.

entries.pullQuote: Order the phở hà nội and drop that raw yolk right in.
entries.blurb: It looks like any strip-mall Vietnamese spot in Greenwood, but Miss Pho cooks well above the setting. Phở hà nội comes brimming with broth and topped with a raw egg yolk, great stirred in or spooned over each bite of noodles and beef shank. The grilled chicken is fragrant with lemongrass, and vegetarians eat just as well here.

entries.pullQuote: Get the fish sauce wings and a lemongrass vermicelli bowl, then shoot some pool.
entries.blurb: Billiard Hoang has long been a Columbia City favorite spread by word of mouth, and it still hasn't slipped. Inside a no-frills pool hall with a roomy dining area, nearly everything on the menu is terrific and inexpensive. Those fish sauce wings are famous for good reason, and the lemongrass chicken vermicelli bowls are big enough to cover two meals.

entries.pullQuote: Go for the wide, hand-pulled noodles and plan to get chili oil everywhere.
entries.blurb: Capitol Hill noodle fans head to Biang Biang Noodles for the broad, belt-like hand-pulled noodles that give the dish its name.

entries.pullQuote: Brisket pho and a gin cocktail in a dark, moody room is the move.
entries.blurb: Ba Bar pulls off a very particular mood, bowls of brisket phở and gin drinks under low light with jazz playing. The towering bar is the first thing you see, tall enough to need a ladder and backed by a giant vintage Vietnamese rock album poster. It feels like a candlelit back alley with nice furniture, and it's open late with a happy hour worth catching.

entries.pullQuote: Go thin and firm on the noodles, extra rich on the broth.
entries.blurb: Expect a line at Ramen DANBO, and expect it to be worth it for Hakata-style tonkotsu this good. The order sheet lets you dial in noodle firmness, broth richness, and spice, so ask for extra fat plus extra karadare if you want it silky and hot.
