Plenty of counter seats make it an easy solo dinner.

entries.pullQuote: A solid Fremont noodle stop when the weather turns and you want broth.
entries.blurb: A casual Fremont ramen shop, Midnite Ramen is an easy call for a bowl of noodles.
Chinese noodle bowls are the focus at Sen Noodle Bar in Ballard.

entries.pullQuote: A dependable Ballard bowl of ramen when the drizzle sets in.
entries.blurb: When the weather turns gray, Arashi Ramen has steaming bowls of noodles waiting in Ballard.

entries.pullQuote: When nobody can decide on dinner, soba and tempura settle the argument.
entries.blurb: Fremont's Kamonegi ends dinner indecision fast with a pairing of soba and tempura that's hard to beat. The noodles are made by hand, the tempura is crisp, and after a long day of choices it feels good to let the kitchen lead. Book it for a low-key date night.

entries.pullQuote: Come solo or as a pair for the tenderest chashu in town.
entries.blurb: Capitol Hill has no shortage of ramen, but Ooink earns its spot with the most tender sliced pork around and some seriously oversized gyoza. The room is small, so plan on going alone or with one friend. It's the bowl you want when you've got a cold.

entries.pullQuote: Order the short rib bowl and ask about the half-chicken special.
entries.blurb: Not every night calls for a dress code, and Phở Bắc in the CID is proof. The vibe is casual and cool, the menu runs from phở to Vietnamese drinking snacks, and parking is actually easy. Brisket and meatball bowls are great, but the huge short rib version and the occasional off-menu bowl with a whole poached half-chicken are the stars.

entries.pullQuote: Bring cash, order the brisket noodles, and add a bowl of congee.
entries.blurb: Two neon signs under the red awning spell it out, congee and noodles, and Mike's Noodle House has been nailing both for years in the CID. Springy egg noodles come loaded with tender brisket and bright greens, while the congee is thick, warm, and soothing. The small dining room hums with chatter and fast service. It's cash only, so stop at the ATM first.

title: Tacos & Mexican
dek: Tacos first, then the wider Mexican rooms.
intro:
Tacos first, then the wider Mexican rooms. Tacos Chukis and Maíz are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Capitol Hill, Pike Place Market, U District without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Capitol Hill, Pike Place Market, U District will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Butternut squash enchiladas and margaritas at the corner of Terry and Harrison.
entries.blurb: Order the butternut squash enchiladas with apricot-chocolate mole rojo, or the brisket tacos on fresh corn tortillas. Weekend brunch runs 10 to 2.

entries.pullQuote: Order the adobada tacos with grilled pineapple and you've made the right call.
entries.blurb: The Broadway taco counter in a building shared with a tattoo shop stopped being a secret long ago, and Tacos Chukis earned the crowds. The house adobada tacos stack marinated grilled pork with avocado salsa, cilantro, onion, and a seared slab of pineapple. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, and it's an ideal stop before a night out.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the seafood for once and eat fresh masa tamales at the market.
entries.blurb: Pike Place pushes everyone toward seafood, but Maíz makes a strong case for corn instead. This bright tortilleria grinds its own nixtamal masa and presses tortillas you'll want to eat every week. That masa shows up in tacos, tamales, and chips with a serious, shattering crunch.

entries.pullQuote: Head here for birria tacos when you're near the University District.
entries.blurb: Birrieria Pepe El Toro, as the name suggests, centers its U District menu on birria and tacos.

entries.pullQuote: Don't leave without the al pastor tacos, and add the boozy fajitas.
entries.blurb: Fogón Cocina Mexicana is loud in the best way, with lime-green walls and cooks pressing fresh tortillas up front. The fajitas get a splash of tequila, beer, and wine, and they're excellent, but al pastor tacos are the real must. It can hold a crowd dinner or a solo seat at the bar.

entries.pullQuote: A sleepy little dining room turning out seriously great Mexican food.
entries.blurb: The room at Alebrijes Kitchen is quiet, with only a few tables, but the kitchen is anything but. Tortilla-wrapped dishes fly out at a steady clip and can rescue the dullest weeknight. Start with the fiery orange salsa and build from there.

entries.pullQuote: Come for wagyu sizzling on a skillet and a hibiscus margarita.
entries.blurb: Carne asada can easily come out thin and leathery, but Asadero treats steak with real respect. Cuts like filet mignon land on a hot skillet, cooked medium rare, alongside corn tortillas, lime, and salsa for building your own tacos. There's chicken, fish, and vegetables on the menu, but the barely pink wagyu with a hibiscus margarita on the side is why you came.

entries.pullQuote: Head here for tacos when Columbia City calls for Tex-Mex.
entries.blurb: Tacos and Tex-Mex plates explain the wait at Jackalope Tex-Mex & Cantina in Columbia City.

entries.pullQuote: Come late for tacos and a tequila list that keeps Capitol Hill up.
entries.blurb: Koko's Restaurant and Tequila Bar serves tacos and Mexican plates on Capitol Hill.

entries.pullQuote: Vegan tortas this good might convert the most committed carnitas fan at lunch.
entries.blurb: Everything at Rojo’s Mexican Food is plant-based, though you'd hardly guess from a menu of asada, chicken, and carnitas-style fillings made in-house. Strong marinades do the heavy lifting, and the jackfruit is a convincing stand-in for braised pork. The small, bright room in Pioneer Square works for a quick lunch with coworkers or a burrito to carry into a Mariners game.

entries.pullQuote: Thick handmade tortillas and that chorizo, potato, and cactus filling are the move.
entries.blurb: Carmelo's Tacos presses its own hefty tortillas and fills them with well-marinated carne asada or a chorizo, potato, and nopal mix that sticks with you. Burrito people should know the cheese gets a quick sear on the griddle before it goes in. It's cheap, it's fast, and the Capitol Hill counter keeps going late.

entries.pullQuote: Easy to drive past for years, and a pleasant shock once you finally stop.
entries.blurb: D' La Santa hides in plain sight on a quiet stretch of north Capitol Hill, and plenty of locals have passed it without noticing. Finding it feels like discovering cash in an old coat pocket. Grab street parking and settle in for a Mexican meal that rewards the detour.

entries.pullQuote: A family Mexican spot on Queen Anne that's already open by breakfast.
entries.blurb: Tacos and other Mexican staples are the business at B & Z Family Mexican Restaurant, with doors open early on Queen Anne.

entries.pullQuote: Come to Ravenna for tacos that are worth a detour across town.
entries.blurb: Mexican cooking comes to Ravenna at Pancita, and the tacos are the reason to go.

entries.pullQuote: Grab tacos at La Palmera when South Lake Union wants something with salsa.
entries.blurb: La Palmera serves tacos and other Mexican staples in South Lake Union.

title: Steakhouses
dek: Steaks, grills, and the rooms that smell like butter.
intro:
Steaks, grills, and the rooms that smell like butter. Joule and The Capital Grille are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Wallingford, Downtown, South Lake Union without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Wallingford, Downtown, South Lake Union will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: A classic steakhouse splurge with lake views that make the bill easier to swallow.
entries.blurb: Right on the water at Lake Union, Daniel's Broiler does old-school steak dinners with big cuts and bigger views. Expect a milestone bill, and plan it around sunset if you can.

entries.pullQuote: Mishima Reserve Wagyu steaks from the Beecher's family.
entries.blurb: Order a Mishima Reserve American Wagyu steak. The company that raises the beef also owns Beecher's, and a butcher case sells the same cuts.

entries.pullQuote: The downtown steakhouse to book when the expense account is paying.
entries.blurb: Metropolitan Grill has been downtown's classic steakhouse since the eighties, all dark wood, big steaks, and expense-account energy. The kitchen stays open late, so it works after a game or a show.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the usual steakhouse script and order the kalbi short rib.
entries.blurb: Joule takes the steakhouse formula and runs it through a Korean lens in Wallingford. Kalbi short rib stands in for the usual steak, sides include rice cakes tossed with chorizo and bitter mustard greens, and the bread basket gives way to scallion pancakes topped with salmon roe. Blue Victorian wallpaper and a great patio make it a strong pick for date night or dinner with parents.

entries.pullQuote: A classic special-occasion steakhouse for impressing your parents, ideally on their dime.
entries.blurb: Downtown, The Capital Grille sticks to the dark-wood steakhouse formula with a big check and the polish that parents tend to appreciate.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up, order a dry-aged steak, and let the tableside show unfold.
entries.blurb: Dim lights, live piano, and servers working tableside carts make El Gaucho the old-school supper club Belltown never outgrew. Get a dry-aged cut with a Caesar tossed right in front of you. Bring a fat budget, since this is a special-occasion check through and through.

entries.pullQuote: The old Bateau room, reopened as Jeffry's steakhouse on Union.
entries.blurb: Bateau and Boat Bar closed, then reopened as Jeffry's in the same Capitol Hill rooms. Dry-aged steaks and steakhouse sides are the menu, and the old bar is now the front door.

title: Seattle Classics & Institutions
dek: The places that already belong to the city.
intro:
The places that already belong to the city. Beecher's Handmade Cheese and Il Terrazzo Carmine are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Pike Place Market, Pioneer Square, Phinney Ridge without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Pike Place Market, Pioneer Square, Phinney Ridge will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Marrow-rich ossobuco and white-jacketed waiters at Pioneer Square's Italian standby since 1984.
entries.blurb: Order the ossobuco, a thick veal shank over buttered fettuccine, after a plate from the antipasto bar. Carmine Smeraldo opened it in 1984.

entries.pullQuote: Go for the lasagna and the cabaret, and fight for a seat on the deck.
entries.blurb: Behind an unmarked pink door in Post Alley, The Pink Door has paired Italian-American comfort food with trapeze acts and cabaret for decades. The summer deck looks out over Elliott Bay, and lasagna is the order. It works for a date, a visiting friend, or a late dinner near Pike Place Market.

entries.pullQuote: Almond croissants and pain au chocolat, baked fresh on-site every day at Pike Place.
entries.blurb: Get the amandine, the almond croissant, and a pain au chocolat, the two bestsellers. Everything is baked on-site, so come early.

entries.pullQuote: A classic steakhouse splurge with lake views that make the bill easier to swallow.
entries.blurb: Right on the water at Lake Union, Daniel's Broiler does old-school steak dinners with big cuts and bigger views. Expect a milestone bill, and plan it around sunset if you can.

entries.pullQuote: New England clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl, with oyster crackers, in Post Alley.
entries.blurb: Get the clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl and add oyster crackers. Skip the smoked salmon chowder.

entries.pullQuote: Get the beef and cheese, eat it standing up, and don't mind the line.
entries.blurb: Since the early nineties, Piroshky Piroshky has filled the market with the smell of baked Russian hand pies, both savory and sweet. The line moves faster than it looks, prices stay friendly, and the counter opens early enough to make breakfast out of a smoked salmon pastry.

entries.pullQuote: Do not leave without the giant shortbread cookie crowned with fudge.
entries.blurb: It's really just a long glass case and a register in Pike Place Market, but everything inside Three Girls Bakery is good. Look for the oversized m&m cookie, the peanut butter cookie hiding a whole Reese's cup, and the raspberry crumble bar. The fudge-topped shortbread dot is mandatory. For lunch, the counter next door makes a salmon salad sandwich.

entries.pullQuote: Order a classic cocktail and the lamb pastitsio, then share a booth.
entries.blurb: Zig Zag Café is known for cocktails, but skipping the Greek food here would be a mistake. Go for the lamb pastitsio, marinated chicken kebabs with a side of tzatziki, and a sesame-rich hummus. Booths force you onto the same side. It stays open late, and happy hour is a classic.

entries.pullQuote: Get the breakfast sandwich and a few coconut cream pie bites to go.
entries.blurb: Dahlia Bakery's pastry case runs deep, but the move is a breakfast sandwich stacked with egg, ham, pepper jack, arugula, and spicy jalapeño aioli. The house English muffins taste nothing like the supermarket kind, which turns out to be a good thing. Seating amounts to a few spots outside, so plan on eating on the go in Belltown.

entries.pullQuote: The downtown steakhouse to book when the expense account is paying.
entries.blurb: Metropolitan Grill has been downtown's classic steakhouse since the eighties, all dark wood, big steaks, and expense-account energy. The kitchen stays open late, so it works after a game or a show.

entries.pullQuote: Goat cheese and lavender fondue and a Palace Burger Royale at Tom Douglas's late bar.
entries.blurb: Order the goat cheese-lavender fondue with apples and grilled focaccia, then the Palace Burger Royale. Grab a stool at the big bar in Belltown.

entries.pullQuote: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.
entries.blurb: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.

entries.pullQuote: Brave the line of tourists for a cup of that famous mac and cheese.
entries.blurb: The nutty, sharp Flagship cheddar from Beecher's Handmade Cheese is in every grocery store in town, but the Pike Place Market shop is where it all gets made. Expect a line packed with curd-sampling tourists at lunch. The reward is a creamy mac and cheese that once made Oprah's list of favorite things, and it's inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: Come for weekend brunch, when the room is loud and the bread is crusty.
entries.blurb: Café Campagne has been cooking French comfort food in Post Alley for more than forty years, and the dining room still channels a Paris bistro with old posters and lamps made from wine bottles. Dinner is mellow and the steak frites are great, but brunch is when this place comes alive. Market crowds spill in to share fluffy egg dishes and good bread over upbeat music, and the check lands in special-occasion range.

entries.pullQuote: Eat a double cheeseburger and a root beer float in the car.
entries.blurb: For a double cheeseburger with fries and a shake on pocket change, Pick-Quick Drive In has you covered. The burgers beat Dick's handily, and you get to sit down while you eat them. Load your friends into the car and get everyone root beer floats made with real soft serve.

entries.pullQuote: A Deluxe, fries, and a chocolate shake is a Seattle rite of passage.
entries.blurb: Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

entries.pullQuote: Order the purple ube pancakes and settle into a booth.
entries.blurb: Seattle mourned hard when Ludi's Restaurant closed in 2019, and the reopening a few years later felt like a homecoming. The Filipino diner now sits a couple of blocks from its old Downtown home, with the same family running the griddle and breakfast served all day. Grab a booth and get the ube pancakes, still as bright purple as ever.

entries.pullQuote: Visit once for the history, then drink your daily coffee somewhere quieter.
entries.blurb: Tourists line up at the market's Starbucks Coffee Company for the vintage logo and bragging rights to the brand's oldest store. It opens early, so arrive before the crowds if you want the souvenir mug without the wait.

entries.pullQuote: Open since 1929, and still pouring when Belltown has gone home.
entries.blurb: The 5 Point Cafe faces the five-way at Tilikum Place, and the doors have been open since 1929. It is the oldest bar in Belltown and also a cafe that can serve breakfast as a nightcap. The city already filed it under dive: a long counter, regulars who do not surrender a stool, and no interest in a redesign. Eat something that can survive a second beer. Then stay later than the plan you walked in with.

entries.pullQuote: Crackly old-fashioned doughnuts under floor-to-ceiling bookshelves at Top Pot's Fifth Avenue flagship.
entries.blurb: Get an old-fashioned, then a pink Feather Boa, and grab a seat by the tall shelves. The Belltown flagship is the one to visit.

entries.pullQuote: Order the sausage and peppers pie and grab a seat at the communal tables.
entries.blurb: Pizza night for adults looks like Serious Pie, a Belltown room with an open kitchen, long shared tables, and lighting that's moody but still lets you see your food. Pies come out oval and blistered, with combinations that are inventive without getting silly. The sausage, peppers, and provolone is the standout, and the crust keeps a satisfying chew under its crisp edges.

entries.pullQuote: Nutmeg-spiked cookie dough ice cream in a hot waffle cone on Capitol Hill.
entries.blurb: Get the cookie dough, a nutmeg-scented flavor that's always on, in a fresh waffle cone. Sample freely; the line moves.

entries.pullQuote: Book a window table upstairs and make lunch the best part of the day.
entries.blurb: Pike Place on a rainy Saturday, elbow to elbow with tourists, rarely feels romantic. Climb the stairs to Matt's in the Market and the whole thing shifts, with seafood and a window view that make the market look charming again. You are paying for the room too, so save it for a date or a lunch you want to remember.

entries.pullQuote: Get onion rings to dunk in fry sauce, plus a mint truffle shake.
entries.blurb: Nobody comes to Red Mill Burgers for gourmet toppings or atmosphere. You come for a charbroiled diner-style patty, cornmeal-crusted onion rings dunked in fry sauce, and a thick shake in flavors like s'mores. Grab a spot at one of the bright red picnic tables, ideally after a hike or a slow afternoon around Phinney Ridge.

entries.pullQuote: Band stickers, sunk leather stools, and cheap beer when a band is loading in.
entries.blurb: Blue Moon Tavern is the U District bar for cheap beer and whatever band is hauling amps through the door. Stickers from old shows cover the walls, the stools have collapsed into their leather, and the booths look sawed from a backyard tree. Sit down if you like a room that remembers its own concerts. Walk on if you wanted a host stand. The Ave has plenty of those, and none of them have this many stickers.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the kids for the jukeboxes and order a breakfast pile.
entries.blurb: Sitting under the West Seattle Bridge, Luna Park Cafe is a longtime greasy spoon packed with kitsch, from vintage lunch boxes to a giant guitar and a creepy clown game. Families fill the booths on weekends, with jukeboxes at the tables to keep kids busy. The food is plainer than the decor, but the breakfast piles are a satisfying bet.

entries.pullQuote: Order a ristretto and sip it slowly, because this is Seattle's espresso benchmark.
entries.blurb: Espresso Vivace pulls the best shots in town, and the obsessive care shows in every cup. The room hums steadily without getting so packed you can't work, and on warm days a roll-up door opens the whole cafe to the sidewalk. Drop your drink on the way out and they'll make you another, no charge.

entries.pullQuote: Alder-smoked salmon on the Lake Union deck is the plate that matters.
entries.blurb: The Wallingford Ivar's faces Lake Union, and alder-smoked salmon justifies stopping at take a deck table. Clam chowder can sit beside it. Come for the water without making a ferry out of dinner.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up, order a dry-aged steak, and let the tableside show unfold.
entries.blurb: Dim lights, live piano, and servers working tableside carts make El Gaucho the old-school supper club Belltown never outgrew. Get a dry-aged cut with a Caesar tossed right in front of you. Bring a fat budget, since this is a special-occasion check through and through.

entries.pullQuote: Bring cash, order the brisket noodles, and add a bowl of congee.
entries.blurb: Two neon signs under the red awning spell it out, congee and noodles, and Mike's Noodle House has been nailing both for years in the CID. Springy egg noodles come loaded with tender brisket and bright greens, while the congee is thick, warm, and soothing. The small dining room hums with chatter and fast service. It's cash only, so stop at the ATM first.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up and celebrate here, where the lake view does half the work.
entries.blurb: Since the fifties, Canlis has been the city's go-to for big celebrations, set in a mid-century modern house perched above Lake Union. Service is famously polished, the tall windows put the water front and center, and the check matches the occasion. Book it for an anniversary, a proposal, or a parents' visit.

entries.pullQuote: Linger over a slow lunch of roast chicken, charcuterie, and frites.
entries.blurb: Steps from the Pike Place frenzy, Le Pichet is a calm French bistro escape. It suits a long lunch, a solo dinner, or any moment the market crowds start wearing you down. Settle in and order cured pork, roast chicken, and a pile of fries.

entries.pullQuote: Book a tatami room, take your shoes off, and let the sake flow.
entries.blurb: Open since before the Model T, Maneki holds the title of Seattle's oldest Japanese restaurant, and it still fills up most nights in the Chinatown-International District. Text ahead for a reservation or expect a very late seating. The main room has a lively hum, but the private tatami rooms are the real move, quiet and closed off with good sushi and plenty of sake.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Caribbean Roast and grab extra napkins, you will need them.
entries.blurb: Seattle's most famous sandwich might be the Caribbean Roast at Paseo, a pile of marinated roast pork and caramelized onions on a toasted baguette. It's gloriously messy, so eat it right away in Fremont rather than letting it sit.

entries.pullQuote: Order both the salmon and tuna samplers, plus a baked crab hand roll.
entries.blurb: A Belltown sushi institution, Shiro's Sushi Restaurant gets everything right, but the samplers are what you will remember. The salmon plate runs through four cuts and preparations, from seared belly to ikura, while the tuna plate shows off lean, marinated, fatty, and negitoro from a single fish. Sit at the counter for omakase at least once, and budget for a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: Order raw oysters by the dozen and grab the wall tables if you brought a date.
entries.blurb: Taylor Shellfish Farms has been growing oysters in Washington for well over a century, and this Pioneer Square bar puts that harvest on ice. Branch out with Dungeness crab or Manila clams once the first round is gone. Couples should claim the tables along the wall, and the bar is there when you would rather face the shells than each other. Happy hour makes a second round easier to justify.

entries.pullQuote: A warm crumpet with ricotta and pesto beats every other quick breakfast at the market.
entries.blurb: Breakfast options at Pike Place Market are thin, which makes The Crumpet Shop so useful. The crumpets are springy and crisp, and their little holes trap toppings like pesto with ricotta or raspberry preserves. Be there while the crumpets are still warm and hardly anything is spent.

entries.pullQuote: Come before sunset, sit at the marble bar, and order oysters by the dozen.
entries.blurb: The Walrus and The Carpenter draws an oyster line in Ballard even though the bay is nowhere in sight. The room feels like a farmhouse that traded livestock for shellfish, and it shines in late afternoon when sunlight bounces off the mirrors. Happy hour helps, and a date here rarely goes wrong.

title: Capitol Hill
dek: Where to eat and drink in Capitol Hill, from a weeknight to a night you bothered to dress for.
intro:
Capitol Hill eats well if you let it. Cafe Lolo and Kajiken cover the cravings, and the walks between them are short enough to stay hungry.

Same craving does not get to take over the page. A neighborhood should feel like a week of dinners, not one cuisine copied down the block.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the parents for Lao food that feels comforting and still like a real night out.
entries.blurb: Capitol Hill's Taurus Ox cooks Lao food with real heat and funk, and it rewards a table that's willing to share. Order sticky rice no matter what. The room works as well for a date as it does for dinner with your folks.

entries.pullQuote: The best tapas in town, and the right call for a double date.
entries.blurb: Galician cooking with a light hand and real restraint is the draw at Maripili Tapas Bar on Capitol Hill. Expect ling cod in a sharp, tangy fish broth, manchego gnocchi, a runny-centered tortilla de patata, and garlic aioli on just about everything. Come with another couple, mark a low-key celebration, or sit solo at the bar and graze. The wine list leans Spanish and Washington.

entries.pullQuote: Ube-and-rum Four Boys tiki drinks under fake tentacles, hidden inside Rumba.
entries.blurb: Order The Four Boys, an ube and rice milk rum drink, and a plate of coconut shrimp. Book ahead; seatings last about 90 minutes.
Get a slice of the pesto pie, the house's famous one, or the House Combo if you want meat. It's been on Capitol Hill since 1995 and stays open until midnight on weekends.

entries.pullQuote: A Deluxe, fries, and a chocolate shake is a Seattle rite of passage.
entries.blurb: Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

entries.pullQuote: Claim the big round booth in back and order garlic knots for the table.
entries.blurb: Dino's Tomato Pie shares owners with Delancey but goes the opposite direction, trading minimalism for dim, old-school pizzeria charm. The charred pies are the draw, and the vodka sauce version is a crowd favorite. Bring your whole crew and try to grab the chandelier booth.

entries.pullQuote: Order the adobada tacos with grilled pineapple and you've made the right call.
entries.blurb: The Broadway taco counter in a building shared with a tattoo shop stopped being a secret long ago, and Tacos Chukis earned the crowds. The house adobada tacos stack marinated grilled pork with avocado salsa, cilantro, onion, and a seared slab of pineapple. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, and it's an ideal stop before a night out.

entries.pullQuote: Share a couple of salads and order the soft wheat porridge at lunch.
entries.blurb: Counter service, folk murals, and fizzy pop music give Cafe Lolo on Capitol Hill a soothing, unhurried feel. The menu goes well past standard soups and sandwiches, with seasonal twists like melon topped with coppa and plum agrodolce, plus pasta made from house-milled flour. At lunch, split a few salads and a bowl of soft wheat porridge, and leave room for the blintzes.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the broth and go all in on a bowl of saucy aburasoba.
entries.blurb: Kajiken specializes in aburasoba, a brothless style of ramen where springy noodles get tossed in a rich sauce at the bottom of the bowl. The Capitol Hill shop keeps things casual.

entries.pullQuote: Splurge on the omakase and do not skip the sake pairing.
entries.blurb: Seattle has no shortage of exclusive omakase counters, but LTD Edition on Capitol Hill deserves priority. The highlight is the uni cart, which delivers a rich sea urchin hand roll like a treat from a street vendor. Chefs explain the story behind every piece, and the sake pairing keeps flowing all night.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Lychee Blossom and bring a first date up to the loft.
entries.blurb: Most trips to Biang Biang Noodles end face-first in a bowl of mala beef, but look up next time. Behind red velvet curtains sits Paper Fan Cocktail Bar, a snug loft dressed with ornate lamps and delicate fans. A few of the tea-based drinks lean medicinal, though the Lychee Blossom, made with gin, green tea, and lemon, drinks bright and easy. It fills up fast, so reserve ahead for a first date.

entries.pullQuote: Book a solo seat for the multi-course kaiseki and sushi meal of your year.
entries.blurb: Reservations for two at Taneda are nearly impossible, but single seats open up far more often, and a solo dinner here is a treat rather than a consolation. The meal runs around two dozen courses of sushi and kaiseki in a tiny spot at the back of a Capitol Hill indoor mall. The check is a special-occasion one, yet it is a strong value among the city omakase counters.

entries.pullQuote: Grab two seats at the long bar for an easy, early-stage date.
entries.blurb: Walking up to Artusi, you catch the smell of grilled bread and olive oil drifting from the kitchen, and the night only gets better inside. This smaller sibling to Spinasse is mostly one big L-shaped counter, and that's where you want to be for sharp cocktails and Italian snacks. It suits a newer date or any night when you want great food in lighter portions.

entries.pullQuote: Order the margherita flatbread and a cocktail for a quiet, easy date.
entries.blurb: Few people seem to know about Single Shot Kitchen & Saloon, which gives a date here some built-in novelty. It's a single handsome room, marble bar included, with candles on every table, oddly calm given the noise of Pike-Pine outside. Keep it simple with cocktails and the excellent flatbread, or celebrate with champagne, plenty of small plates, and a good piece of fish.

entries.pullQuote: Order the espresso float and discover that root beer belongs in coffee.
entries.blurb: The baristas at Ghost Note Coffee reach for cocktail shakers as often as steam wands. That precision shows in a smoked grapefruit and rosemary cold espresso served in a coupe, and in a malty mocha shake brightened with orange peel. The real showstopper is the espresso float, which pairs iced latte with local root beer and vegan cream.

entries.pullQuote: An early Capitol Hill breakfast here makes an easy win with visiting parents.
entries.blurb: Opening early for breakfast and brunch, Harry’s Fine Foods serves New American cooking that suits a meal with the folks.

entries.pullQuote: Order every pasta you can justify, starting with the buttery tajarin.
entries.blurb: For a splurge Italian dinner in Seattle, Spinasse sets the bar, with handmade Piedmontese pasta and service that runs like clockwork. The Capitol Hill dining room mixes reclaimed wood with a sleek marble bar and an open kitchen where you can watch the noodles being made. Expect a special-occasion check, and know the kitchen keeps going late.

entries.pullQuote: Order the plain croissant, a steady classic that gets every essential right.
entries.blurb: The French Guys works out of a little stone cottage on Capitol Hill that looks lifted from a storybook. Their plain croissant isn't the flakiest or richest around, but it's buttery, crunchy, and dependable in a way you'll come to count on. It opens early, and prices are gentle.

entries.pullQuote: An early Capitol Hill coffee stop with a little Mexican market attached.
entries.blurb: Bonito Cafe Y Mercadito pours coffee and sells Mexican goods on Capitol Hill, opening early and staying gentle on a weekday budget.

entries.pullQuote: An early-opening Capitol Hill coffee shop for the commute or a slow morning.
entries.blurb: Copper Tree Coffee House opens early for Capitol Hill coffee runs, and the prices stay low.
Donna's pours drinks on the Hill and makes the cut among the neighborhood's better bars.

entries.pullQuote: Dairy-free scoops so good you'll forget anything was missing in the first place.
entries.blurb: Frankie & Jo's makes Seattle's best ice cream without a drop of dairy or a speck of wheat. The cultured crème fraîche flavor, swirled with berries and studded with lemon cake, is unforgettable, and oat milk vanilla loaded with brown sugar blondies is close behind. Get your scoops in a house maple oat waffle cone, and know the Hill shop stays open late.

entries.pullQuote: Brave the morning line for a twice-baked almond croissant you won't want to share.
entries.blurb: Bakery Nouveau's twice-baked almond croissant is the order, messy with toasted almond slivers and powdered sugar. It's worth braving the long morning line, claiming a table, and settling in with a hot latte. Lunch holds up too, and the croque monsieur ranks with the best ham sandwiches in town.

entries.pullQuote: Go for the wide, hand-pulled noodles and plan to get chili oil everywhere.
entries.blurb: Capitol Hill noodle fans head to Biang Biang Noodles for the broad, belt-like hand-pulled noodles that give the dish its name.

entries.pullQuote: Don't leave without the al pastor tacos, and add the boozy fajitas.
entries.blurb: Fogón Cocina Mexicana is loud in the best way, with lime-green walls and cooks pressing fresh tortillas up front. The fajitas get a splash of tequila, beer, and wine, and they're excellent, but al pastor tacos are the real must. It can hold a crowd dinner or a solo seat at the bar.

entries.pullQuote: Buy a bag of everything bagels and a tub of the spicy scallion schmear.
entries.blurb: Seattle's bagel scene changed when Mt. Bagel showed up selling them whole, with tubs of schmear to take home. Inside, they're malty, chewy, and a little sweet, and they hold up great frozen and toasted later. The crust's crackle can vary, but the flavor never does, especially on the garlicky everything.

entries.pullQuote: Come late for tacos and a tequila list that keeps Capitol Hill up.
entries.blurb: Koko's Restaurant and Tequila Bar serves tacos and Mexican plates on Capitol Hill.
Sushi and drinks are the draw at Star Sushi & Bar on Capitol Hill.

entries.pullQuote: Rooftop brunch here is worth a sunburn, so bring sunscreen and a big appetite.
entries.blurb: Terra Plata's rooftop garden on Capitol Hill turns brunch into a long, sunny affair, with a Spanish-leaning breakfast that kicks off nicely with patatas bravas. The roof gets brutally hot in summer, so plan accordingly. Come back around sunset for wine and snacks, which is when the waffled potato chips with truffle salt appear. It also makes a strong date spot.

entries.pullQuote: Book it for date night when everyone at the table is craving Italian.
entries.blurb: Cornelly makes a strong case for an Italian dinner date on Capitol Hill.

entries.pullQuote: Pick a heat level one notch below your ego and order the sliders.
entries.blurb: Nashville-style hot chicken tenders and sliders make up nearly the whole menu at Dave's Hot Chicken, with spice that runs from mild to genuinely painful. The Capitol Hill counter keeps it cheap.

entries.pullQuote: The Fairfax on a warm brioche bun fixes almost any rough morning.
entries.blurb: The LA egg sandwich chain Eggslut landed on Capitol Hill, and the Fairfax, with soft scrambled eggs, chives, cheddar, and sriracha mayo on a brioche bun, is the order regulars make. Doors open early, and the bill stays gentle enough for a weekday treat.

entries.pullQuote: Natural wine nerds, this is your clubhouse, deep cuts and murky pours included.
entries.blurb: Remember the Juice Club pop-up? Its crew now runs Otherworld, a Capitol Hill natural wine bar built for glou-glou devotees. Prices hang on a deli-style felt board, the shelves are lined with bottles sporting arty labels, and the music runs funky and obscure. Settle in with small glasses of something cloudy, and know the night runs long here.

entries.pullQuote: Order the BEC on a poppy roll, then grab a pastry for later.
entries.blurb: Tucked into a house in north Capitol Hill, Volunteer Park Cafe & Pantry would be worth a visit for pastries alone, like tahini caramel bars and buckwheat chocolate chunk cookies. The breakfast sandwich is the real star, with thin folded eggs, barely crisp bacon, and melty American cheese on a toasted house poppy seed roll. Laptops aren't allowed on weekends.

entries.pullQuote: Brisket pho and a gin cocktail in a dark, moody room is the move.
entries.blurb: Ba Bar pulls off a very particular mood, bowls of brisket phở and gin drinks under low light with jazz playing. The towering bar is the first thing you see, tall enough to need a ladder and backed by a giant vintage Vietnamese rock album poster. It feels like a candlelit back alley with nice furniture, and it's open late with a happy hour worth catching.

entries.pullQuote: Go thin and firm on the noodles, extra rich on the broth.
entries.blurb: Expect a line at Ramen DANBO, and expect it to be worth it for Hakata-style tonkotsu this good. The order sheet lets you dial in noodle firmness, broth richness, and spice, so ask for extra fat plus extra karadare if you want it silky and hot. Plenty of counter seats make it an easy solo dinner.
For pizza on Capitol Hill, Capitale Pizzeria lands on the neighborhood's shortlist of reliable pies.

entries.pullQuote: Bring a group to brunch and order the Sichuan wings for the table.
entries.blurb: Street food from all over the map shares one menu on Capitol Hill, from Burmese and Jamaican to South African and Chinese. It should be a mess, but Nue makes every detour land. Weekend mornings here swap the benedict for tocino and fried rice, harissa-laced octopus, and pineapple-coconut cornbread. A pile of crunchy Sichuan wings never hurts either.

entries.pullQuote: A quick Korean counter on Capitol Hill for a filling bowl at lunch.
entries.blurb: Korean bowls come over the counter at Seoul Bowl Co, a quick-service stop on Capitol Hill.

entries.pullQuote: A Capitol Hill option when the group is craving Latin American food.
entries.blurb: On Capitol Hill, Bad Chancla is where to go for Latin American cooking.

title: Pike Place Market
dek: Where to eat and drink in Pike Place Market, from a weeknight to a night you bothered to dress for.
intro:
Pike Place Market eats well if you let it. Anchorhead Coffee and Pasta Casalinga cover the cravings, and the walks between them are short enough to stay hungry.

Same craving does not get to take over the page. A neighborhood should feel like a week of dinners, not one cuisine copied down the block.

entries.pullQuote: Go for the lasagna and the cabaret, and fight for a seat on the deck.
entries.blurb: Behind an unmarked pink door in Post Alley, The Pink Door has paired Italian-American comfort food with trapeze acts and cabaret for decades. The summer deck looks out over Elliott Bay, and lasagna is the order. It works for a date, a visiting friend, or a late dinner near Pike Place Market.

entries.pullQuote: Get the steamed barbecue pork bao and eat it walking through the stalls.
entries.blurb: Swing by in the late morning, before the market fully wakes up, and you'll catch the crew at Mee Sum Pastry folding potstickers and pinching shumai. Grab an assortment and snack your way through Pike Place. It's all good, but the steamed pork hum bao is the order regulars make, and it's open early and inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: For the city's best sushi, book the counter and let the chefs decide.
entries.blurb: Skip the waterfront oyster crawl and the fish and chips shops, because the finest seafood in town is at Sushi Kashiba. Shiro Kashiba, who trained under Jiro Ono, opened it at the edge of Pike Place Market in 2015 after leaving his namesake restaurant. Expect impeccable nigiri and a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: Cioppino in a candlelit grotto under Pike Place.
entries.blurb: Order the cioppino or the rigatoni Bolognese in this candlelit room down a cobblestone alley under the market, open for more than 50 years.

entries.pullQuote: New England clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl, with oyster crackers, in Post Alley.
entries.blurb: Get the clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl and add oyster crackers. Skip the smoked salmon chowder.

entries.pullQuote: A latte and a Theo chocolate chunk cookie upstairs in the Corner Market building.
entries.blurb: Order a latte and the chocolate chunk cookie, made with 70% Theo chocolate and Maldon salt. Take the stairs to the top floor at First and Pike.

entries.pullQuote: Get the beef and cheese, eat it standing up, and don't mind the line.
entries.blurb: Since the early nineties, Piroshky Piroshky has filled the market with the smell of baked Russian hand pies, both savory and sweet. The line moves faster than it looks, prices stay friendly, and the counter opens early enough to make breakfast out of a smoked salmon pastry.

entries.pullQuote: Get the pomodoro with burrata and leave space for the ricotta crostata.
entries.blurb: Inside Pike Place Market, Pasta Casalinga turns out handmade bowls that would hold their own in Italy. The rotating menu pulls from ocean, garden, and farm, think rigatoni with lamb and juniper ragu or spaghettoni tossed in kale pesto. The best bowl is the simplest one, pomodoro topped with a cool spoonful of burrata. If the ricotta chocolate crostata is on, order it, and bring your parents.

entries.pullQuote: Head up to the rooftop for a late drink above Pike Place.
entries.blurb: Lonely Siren brings Portuguese cooking to Pike Place Market, with a roof deck and a kitchen that runs late.

entries.pullQuote: Order the rosemary brown sugar sazerac and a bowl of spicy mac.
entries.blurb: Tucked down Post Alley past the gum wall, Alibi Room pours serious cocktails steps from the Market. Any well drink is fair game, but the house specialties are the move, especially a sazerac sweetened with brown sugar and rosemary. Pair it with the spicy mac and cheese.

entries.pullQuote: Cool off between Pike Place errands with a cup of tangy frozen yogurt.
entries.blurb: Frozen yogurt and gelato come cheap at HELLENIKA Cultured Creamery inside the arcade.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a cup of gelato here while you wander the Market.
entries.blurb: Italian-style ice cream justifies stopping at stop at Bottega Italiana inside the arcade.

entries.pullQuote: Get the blackened salmon sandwich with rosemary mayo and a cup of chowder.
entries.blurb: Squeezing through Pike Place crowds sounds like a bad lunch plan, but Market Grill makes it pay off. The counter sits right in the middle of the action, where the cooks sear a blackened salmon sandwich slicked in rosemary mayo. Add the herby clam chowder on the side. Solo diners can usually snag a stool, while groups should take it to go.

entries.pullQuote: Brave the line of tourists for a cup of that famous mac and cheese.
entries.blurb: The nutty, sharp Flagship cheddar from Beecher's Handmade Cheese is in every grocery store in town, but the Pike Place Market shop is where it all gets made. Expect a line packed with curd-sampling tourists at lunch. The reward is a creamy mac and cheese that once made Oprah's list of favorite things, and it's inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: Come for weekend brunch, when the room is loud and the bread is crusty.
entries.blurb: Café Campagne has been cooking French comfort food in Post Alley for more than forty years, and the dining room still channels a Paris bistro with old posters and lamps made from wine bottles. Dinner is mellow and the steak frites are great, but brunch is when this place comes alive. Market crowds spill in to share fluffy egg dishes and good bread over upbeat music, and the check lands in special-occasion range.

entries.pullQuote: Go hungry and order a gravy-smothered biscuit sandwich with plenty of hot sauce.
entries.blurb: Biscuit Bitch serves hefty breakfast biscuits stacked with fillings, and the whole menu leans into its trailer-park-to-table joke. Try The Canadian Bitch, built on banana and maple peanut butter, or the Bitchwich loaded with sausage, egg, cheese, and gravy plus hot sauce.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a cheap early breakfast here before the market crowds arrive.
entries.blurb: Opening early with inexpensive cafe fare, Kitchen & Market doubles as a small grocery inside Pike Place Market.

entries.pullQuote: Order the purple ube pancakes and settle into a booth.
entries.blurb: Seattle mourned hard when Ludi's Restaurant closed in 2019, and the reopening a few years later felt like a homecoming. The Filipino diner now sits a couple of blocks from its old Downtown home, with the same family running the griddle and breakfast served all day. Grab a booth and get the ube pancakes, still as bright purple as ever.

entries.pullQuote: Visit once for the history, then drink your daily coffee somewhere quieter.
entries.blurb: Tourists line up at the market's Starbucks Coffee Company for the vintage logo and bragging rights to the brand's oldest store. It opens early, so arrive before the crowds if you want the souvenir mug without the wait.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the seafood for once and eat fresh masa tamales at the market.
entries.blurb: Pike Place pushes everyone toward seafood, but Maíz makes a strong case for corn instead. This bright tortilleria grinds its own nixtamal masa and presses tortillas you'll want to eat every week. That masa shows up in tacos, tamales, and chips with a serious, shattering crunch.

entries.pullQuote: Fine for a patio break with visitors, but skip the pricey crab.
entries.blurb: Up at the north end of Pike Place, Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder caters to tourists with a menu that comes and goes in quality. The fried fish is fine, and the bacon-y clam chowder with its Goldfish-style crackers is the strongest play. A breezy patio over Elliott Bay makes it a decent rest stop with guests.

entries.pullQuote: Order the pork belly burnt ends and a whiskey, then stay for another round.
entries.blurb: Climb the stairs above the market and you'll find Radiator Whiskey, a small, dark room with a deep whiskey list and food built to absorb it. Think burnt ends, tots smothered in gravy with a fried egg, and marrow bones set up for a luge. Reserve ahead for the smoked pig's head, though landing a table on a Friday is usually painless.

entries.pullQuote: An easy, cheap snack stop for grazing your way through the Market.
entries.blurb: Snack on cheap popcorn from Cobb's Pike Place Popcorn while you wander the Market.

entries.pullQuote: Book a window table upstairs and make lunch the best part of the day.
entries.blurb: Pike Place on a rainy Saturday, elbow to elbow with tourists, rarely feels romantic. Climb the stairs to Matt's in the Market and the whole thing shifts, with seafood and a window view that make the market look charming again. You are paying for the room too, so save it for a date or a lunch you want to remember.

entries.pullQuote: Book a window table at sunset and let the Sound do half the romancing.
entries.blurb: Down a flight of stairs at the back of the market, Place Pigalle Restaurant and Bar hides a small French dining room with big windows over Elliott Bay. The check is a special-occasion one, but the view, the quiet, and the French cooking make a date night feel planned well in advance.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap and cheerful pastry stop when you're wandering the Market.
entries.blurb: Anyone wandering Pike Place Market can grab an inexpensive pastry at Baxter & Frost.

entries.pullQuote: Go early on a weekday, graze the stalls, and watch the fish fly.
entries.blurb: Seattle's famous public market opens early, and a weekday morning is the best time to wander before the crowds arrive. Pike Place Market rewards grazing, with produce, flowers, baked goods, and seafood counters at every turn.

entries.pullQuote: An early pastry stop for market wanderers who want something flaky and cheap.
entries.blurb: Inexpensive pastries and an early opening make Pufftown Bakehouse an easy first stop on a Pike Place Market morning.

entries.pullQuote: A late-night Pike Place stop for a cocktail or a glass of wine.
entries.blurb: Near Pike Place Market, The Dressing Room pours cocktails and wine until late.

entries.pullQuote: Chocolate lovers should stop here for bars made from the bean up.
entries.blurb: In the market, Indi Chocolate makes its own chocolate from scratch and sells bars and other treats at the counter.

entries.pullQuote: House beers and plenty of tables when your whole crew hits the market.
entries.blurb: In the market, Old Stove Brewing pours its own beer and has room for a big group.

entries.pullQuote: Sit at the counter, fill out the card, and order cold sake.
entries.blurb: Downtown is short on quality sushi lunches, so Sugo Hand Roll Bar at Pike Place fills a real gap with hand rolls built on excellent fish. The four-sided counter looks a bit like an airport bar, yet the room manages to feel calm and lively at once, with blowtorches searing king salmon on a pink salt block. Mark your order on the sheet at your seat and get a carafe of chilled sake.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a poke bowl at the market when you need a quick lunch.
entries.blurb: At Pike Place Market, Wild Fish Poke serves Hawaiian-style poke from a counter.

entries.pullQuote: An easy Market brunch stop that's open before most shops roll up their gates.
entries.blurb: Breakfast and brunch start early at Bacco Cafe, a morning stop inside the arcade.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a cinnamon roll early, before the Market crowds take over.
entries.blurb: Among the market stalls, Cinnamon Works sells big, inexpensive pastries starting first thing in the morning.

entries.pullQuote: Linger over a slow lunch of roast chicken, charcuterie, and frites.
entries.blurb: Steps from the Pike Place frenzy, Le Pichet is a calm French bistro escape. It suits a long lunch, a solo dinner, or any moment the market crowds start wearing you down. Settle in and order cured pork, roast chicken, and a pile of fries.

entries.pullQuote: Order the salmon sinigang, follow the signs, and don't rush the cook.
entries.blurb: In a quiet corner of Pike Place Market, a Filipino counter is wallpapered with handwritten signs pinned up by clothespins, each one warning you to behave. They seem gruff at first and get funnier the longer you read. Oriental Mart backs up the attitude with the best lunch in the market and some of the city's finest Filipino cooking. You can get in before work and won't cost much.

entries.pullQuote: Duck in for a spiked mule when the market crowds get to be too much.
entries.blurb: After a couple of hours dodging tourists at Pike Place, Rachel's Ginger Beer is a welcome breather. The house ginger beer comes plain or in flavors like pink guava and cucumber tarragon, and any of them can be turned into a boozy mule. It's cheap, it's open late, and it's right in the middle of everything.

entries.pullQuote: A warm crumpet with ricotta and pesto beats every other quick breakfast at the market.
entries.blurb: Breakfast options at Pike Place Market are thin, which makes The Crumpet Shop so useful. The crumpets are springy and crisp, and their little holes trap toppings like pesto with ricotta or raspberry preserves. Be there while the crumpets are still warm and hardly anything is spent.

title: Downtown
dek: Where to eat and drink in Downtown, from a weeknight to a night you bothered to dress for.
intro:
Downtown eats well if you let it. Anchorhead Coffee and Carmine's cover the cravings, and the walks between them are short enough to stay hungry.

Same craving does not get to take over the page. A neighborhood should feel like a week of dinners, not one cuisine copied down the block.

entries.pullQuote: A latte and a Theo chocolate chunk cookie upstairs in the Corner Market building.
entries.blurb: Order a latte and the chocolate chunk cookie, made with 70% Theo chocolate and Maldon salt. Take the stairs to the top floor at First and Pike.

entries.pullQuote: Rigatoni Bolognese under the soaring rotunda windows downtown.
entries.blurb: Order the rigatoni Bolognese, a Carmine family classic, or the newer osso buco ravioli. It's the Smeraldo family's downtown room, after Il Terrazzo.

entries.pullQuote: A sharp downtown espresso stop for people who actually care about the beans.
entries.blurb: Downtown commuters get an early start with Olympia Coffee and its well-regarded roasts.

entries.pullQuote: The downtown steakhouse to book when the expense account is paying.
entries.blurb: Metropolitan Grill has been downtown's classic steakhouse since the eighties, all dark wood, big steaks, and expense-account energy. The kitchen stays open late, so it works after a game or a show.

entries.pullQuote: Request glass-side seating at sunset and let the Elliott Bay view do the work.
entries.blurb: Inside the Four Seasons downtown, Goldfinch Tavern serves polished American food with big windows facing the water. It opens early for breakfast and keeps the bar going late, so the room suits a morning meeting or a nightcap.

entries.pullQuote: Downtown workers, the quaffle and a spiced cold brew beat any lobby breakfast.
entries.blurb: Downtown is short on morning options that aren't chain coffee or a sad pastry, which makes Anchorhead Coffee a real find. Grab a small banana bread or a biscuit sandwich, or go big with the quaffle, a cinnamon roll, croissant, and waffle hybrid. The honey bunches of cold brew, with burnt honey, cinnamon, and oat milk, is the drink to get.

entries.pullQuote: Adjaruli khachapuri, a cheese bread boat with a runny yolk, baked to order downtown.
entries.blurb: Order the Adjaruli and swirl the yolk and butter into the cheese, then tear the crust to dip. Each boat is baked to order in about 15 minutes.

entries.pullQuote: Order the rice gelato, which tastes like rice pudding straight from the freezer.
entries.blurb: Gelatiamo scoops the city's best gelato and gets you as close to a Roman vacation as Downtown Seattle allows. Every flavor is solid, stracciatella included, but the rice flavor is the one people talk about. It's creamy, gently sweet, and refreshingly free of cinnamon.

entries.pullQuote: Bucatini and bone-marrow meatballs at Two Union Square.
entries.blurb: Get the bucatini with beef-and-ricotta meatballs in a marrow-enriched tomato sauce. The pasta is made fresh daily, and the pizza dough proofs for three days.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a charred, chewy slice and shake on more garlic than seems reasonable.
entries.blurb: Ignore the name, because Post Alley Pizza isn't actually in the market. It's a dependable downtown lunch slice with a crust that manages to be both blistered and chewy, plus dipping sauces like house ranch and a Calabrian chili buffalo. The real perk is a shaker of granulated garlic, which almost no other slice shop in town bothers to put out.

entries.pullQuote: A polished downtown pick for pan-Asian plates before a show or meeting.
entries.blurb: Wild Ginger Kitchen serves Asian fusion dishes in a polished downtown dining room.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap, early-opening downtown cafe for coffee before work.
entries.blurb: Downtown coffee from The Shop by Porter starts early in the morning and won't cost much.

entries.pullQuote: Rooftop cocktails and smoked salmon dip above Pike Place at the Thompson Hotel.
entries.blurb: Order a Seattle After Dark, with brown butter-washed rye and rum, and the smoked salmon dip. Expect a 20% service charge.

entries.pullQuote: Use it for happy hour and stick around for the hourly drink wheel.
entries.blurb: Von's 1000Spirits lives up to its name with a huge bar and a long list of bottles. The sourdough pizza and pasta are solid and the cocktails are better, but this is mostly a happy hour or post-day-drinking lunch move. Every hour they spin a wheel to pick the drink special, and it stays open late.

entries.pullQuote: Come for pico-topped rolls and sukiyaki tacos when you want a flashy dinner.
entries.blurb: Japonessa Sushi Cocina mixes sushi with Latin flavors, so rolls get salsa and tortillas get filled with beef sukiyaki. It's loud, touristy, and busy even midweek, but the fish is reliably good. Happy hour and a late kitchen make it an easy Downtown call.

entries.pullQuote: A classic downtown hotel lounge for a cold martini and quiet conversation.
entries.blurb: Inside the Mayflower Park Hotel downtown, Oliver's Lounge has a long reputation for its martinis. Big windows look out on the street, and it's a calm spot for a drink after shopping.

entries.pullQuote: A downtown cocktail bar that's already open when most bars are still asleep.
entries.blurb: Downtown, The Fonté Bar mixes pricier cocktails and opens its doors early in the day.

entries.pullQuote: Sesame-honey fried chicken and hush puppies in The State Hotel by Pike.
entries.blurb: Order the buttermilk fried chicken with sesame honey and the hush puppies. Breakfast starts at 7 in this tall, brass-trimmed room steps from Pike Place.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up, sit at the bar, and order the lamb agnolotti with fries.
entries.blurb: The George brings real glamour to the renovated Fairmont Olympic Hotel, and it's somewhere you can dress up without feeling silly. The menu runs long, from seafood towers to pasta, and not all of it lands, so skip the steak and duck. Go for lamb agnolotti in parmesan broth and a side of fries with some bubbles. Expect a special-occasion bill.

entries.pullQuote: A cheap downtown hot dog when lunch needs to happen in five minutes.
entries.blurb: Dog in the Park handles quick, inexpensive franks for Downtown lunch breaks.

entries.pullQuote: Grab a marble barstool under the neon glow and order something classic.
entries.blurb: The Diller Room has been pouring drinks in some form for more than a hundred years, which puts it ahead of the Space Needle. At night the marble bar picks up light from the old Diller Hotel neon sign, and the menu mixes old standards with modern cocktails. The crowd is friendly and very Seattle.

entries.pullQuote: Lobster mac and cheese beside a 30-foot tower of wine near Benaroya Hall.
entries.blurb: Order the Maine lobster mac and cheese and a glass from the long list. The wine tower anchors the room; happy hour runs weekdays 2 to 5.

entries.pullQuote: A downtown drinks room for a nightcap that turns into a second round.
entries.blurb: Founders Club mixes polished drinks in the Downtown core and keeps the bar open late.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the laptop, order a matcha latte, and camp out all day.
entries.blurb: If you need somewhere to work all day without going hungry, Mr West Cafe Bar Downtown is the answer. The room is all plants, marble, and gold accents, which suits curried avocado toast and a green tea latte. Lunch brings polished panini and salads, and later on there are cheese boards and frozen wine slushies.

entries.pullQuote: Order the matcha parfait with cake on top and call it lunch.
entries.blurb: After a rough morning, sometimes the fix is sitting alone with soft serve in a waffle cone crowned with a whole slice of cake. Nana's Green Tea, a matcha-everything Japanese cafe downtown, is happy to make that your midday meal.

entries.pullQuote: A classic special-occasion steakhouse for impressing your parents, ideally on their dime.
entries.blurb: Downtown, The Capital Grille sticks to the dark-wood steakhouse formula with a big check and the polish that parents tend to appreciate.

entries.pullQuote: Claim a stool along the round center bar and play hotel guest for an evening.
entries.blurb: Afternoon Tea at Fairmont Olympic Hotel sits inside one of downtown's grandest old lobbies, where it's easy to pretend you have a room upstairs. Skip the hidden speakeasy and take a stool at the circular counter at the center of the room. The cocktails hold up well, with pairings like cognac and orgeat or tequila with chocolate bitters.

entries.pullQuote: Book it for the skyline views and a dinner that feels like an occasion.
entries.blurb: High up in the Lotte Hotel, Charlotte Restaurant & Lounge pairs New American plates with sweeping views over downtown and the water. The bill belongs to a celebration, so save it for anniversaries and visiting parents who love a view.

entries.pullQuote: Take a bar stool, order a dirty martini, and work through a dozen oysters.
entries.blurb: Inside the Fairmont Olympic, SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR is an old-school room that smells faintly of brine and polished leather. Happy hour knocks the price of local raw oysters way down, and the baked ones topped with toasted brioche and lemony herb butter deserve a spot in your order. The space was a haberdashery in the early twentieth century, and it still has that buttoned-up charm.

entries.pullQuote: Book it before a show when you want a stylish dinner steps from the theater.
entries.blurb: Across from the Paramount Theatre, The Carlile Room serves New American plates in a colorful downtown room that's handy for pre-show meals.

entries.pullQuote: A walk-up espresso window for a fast, cheap shot on the way in.
entries.blurb: From a tiny walk-up window near the Denny Triangle, Monorail Espresso pulls inexpensive shots starting early.

entries.pullQuote: A dependable downtown Italian dining room for pasta before a night out.
entries.blurb: Downtown's Tulio has been serving Italian food out of the Hotel Vintage for decades, and pasta is the draw.

entries.pullQuote: An early-opening downtown spot for an American breakfast before a busy day.
entries.blurb: Downtown's The Hart and The Hunter serves American food starting before the street is busy.

entries.pullQuote: A sleek downtown hotel lounge for a late cocktail after dinner.
entries.blurb: Inside the downtown W hotel, W Living Room Bar pours pricier cocktails late into the night.

entries.pullQuote: A downtown Mediterranean dining room that starts serving before nine.
entries.blurb: Downtown early birds can get Mediterranean food at Andaluca Restaurant, which opens in time for a breakfast meeting.

entries.pullQuote: An easy early espresso stop for anyone working downtown.
entries.blurb: Downtown commuters can count on Artly for inexpensive coffee starting first thing in the morning.

entries.pullQuote: Take visitors up for a cocktail with the city spread out below.
entries.blurb: Fog Room pours drinks on a Downtown rooftop with skyline views, and you can linger past eleven.

title: Belltown
dek: Where to eat and drink in Belltown, from a weeknight to a night you bothered to dress for.
intro:
Belltown eats well if you let it. Sushi by Scratch Restaurants and Shomon cover the cravings, and the walks between them are short enough to stay hungry.

Same craving does not get to take over the page. A neighborhood should feel like a week of dinners, not one cuisine copied down the block.

entries.pullQuote: French-spirit cocktails from Erik Hakkinen on First Ave.
entries.blurb: Erik Hakkinen's Belltown bar leans on cognac and calvados, and it's open until 1 or 2am every night.

entries.pullQuote: Mushroom fettuccine beside the Belltown courtyard fountain, since 1994.
entries.blurb: Order the fettuccine ai funghi, the best seller, or the squid-ink linguine with salmon. There's been a table by the courtyard fountain since 1994.

entries.pullQuote: Book the back room for a date fueled by salmon nigiri and sake.
entries.blurb: Before Momiji, there was Umi Sake House, and the first one is still the pick. Ask for the back dining room, which feels like a bamboo garden turned lounge, and order a nigiri sampler plus rolls with seared snow crab or spicy yellowtail. Big groups can usually book even the night before, and the happy hour and late kitchen help.

entries.pullQuote: Get the breakfast sandwich and a few coconut cream pie bites to go.
entries.blurb: Dahlia Bakery's pastry case runs deep, but the move is a breakfast sandwich stacked with egg, ham, pepper jack, arugula, and spicy jalapeño aioli. The house English muffins taste nothing like the supermarket kind, which turns out to be a good thing. Seating amounts to a few spots outside, so plan on eating on the go in Belltown.

entries.pullQuote: Goat cheese and lavender fondue and a Palace Burger Royale at Tom Douglas's late bar.
entries.blurb: Order the goat cheese-lavender fondue with apples and grilled focaccia, then the Palace Burger Royale. Grab a stool at the big bar in Belltown.

entries.pullQuote: Belltown sushi that can stand alone on a crowded list of contenders.
entries.blurb: FOB Sushi Bar handles raw fish in Belltown and earns a mention among the city's better sushi spots.

entries.pullQuote: Naturally leavened sourdough and pastries at the original 1993 Macrina bakery in Belltown.
entries.blurb: Take home a loaf of the sourdough or the Rustic Potato bread, and eat a pastry with coffee here. This Belltown cafe is where Macrina began in 1993.

entries.pullQuote: Lobster risotto and truffle-sausage gnocchi at a candlelit Westlake Italian open until 11.
entries.blurb: Order the lobster tail risotto with shrimp bisque, or the house gnocchi with black truffle and sausage. Dinner runs nightly from 3 to 11.

entries.pullQuote: Come for the wings, stay for the chaos, and catch the game if you must.
entries.blurb: Vindicktive Wings looks like a generic Belltown sports bar at first, all big booths and TVs, but people show up here for wings first and the game second. Give it time and the room starts to feel like a great college party, with loud music and bartenders who remember you. The wings are inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: Go hungry and order a gravy-smothered biscuit sandwich with plenty of hot sauce.
entries.blurb: Biscuit Bitch serves hefty breakfast biscuits stacked with fillings, and the whole menu leans into its trailer-park-to-table joke. Try The Canadian Bitch, built on banana and maple peanut butter, or the Bitchwich loaded with sausage, egg, cheese, and gravy plus hot sauce.

entries.pullQuote: Open since 1929, and still pouring when Belltown has gone home.
entries.blurb: The 5 Point Cafe faces the five-way at Tilikum Place, and the doors have been open since 1929. It is the oldest bar in Belltown and also a cafe that can serve breakfast as a nightcap. The city already filed it under dive: a long counter, regulars who do not surrender a stool, and no interest in a redesign. Eat something that can survive a second beer. Then stay later than the plan you walked in with.
Build a salmon or tuna bowl over rice or greens, and finish it with the house FOB sauce, a Hawaiian shoyu blend, and the zesty mango.

entries.pullQuote: Crackly old-fashioned doughnuts under floor-to-ceiling bookshelves at Top Pot's Fifth Avenue flagship.
entries.blurb: Get an old-fashioned, then a pink Feather Boa, and grab a seat by the tall shelves. The Belltown flagship is the one to visit.

entries.pullQuote: Square pies with crispy edges, best split with a friend in Belltown.
entries.blurb: Thick, square pies are the draw at Moto Pizza in Belltown, a casual pick for pizza night.

entries.pullQuote: Start a Belltown night with a cocktail here before heading to dinner.
entries.blurb: Cocktails lead the menu at House Of Eve, a bar in Belltown.

entries.pullQuote: Order the sausage and peppers pie and grab a seat at the communal tables.
entries.blurb: Pizza night for adults looks like Serious Pie, a Belltown room with an open kitchen, long shared tables, and lighting that's moody but still lets you see your food. Pies come out oval and blistered, with combinations that are inventive without getting silly. The sausage, peppers, and provolone is the standout, and the crust keeps a satisfying chew under its crisp edges.

entries.pullQuote: Rally a big group here to watch the game and eat bar food.
entries.blurb: Game days in Belltown mean a crowd at Buckley's, a sports bar with plenty of room for groups and a kitchen open late.

entries.pullQuote: Book the counter for a parade of nigiri and a seriously special night.
entries.blurb: Sushi by Scratch Restaurants runs an intimate omakase counter in Belltown where chefs work through a long series of creative nigiri right in front of you. It's a special-occasion check, seatings run late, and it's a strong move for impressing visiting parents.

entries.pullQuote: Snag a counter seat for eight courses and a crab nugget you'll crave later.
entries.blurb: From the team behind Shiro's, Shomon gives Seattle omakase a looser, livelier spin. Chefs move around an open kitchen chatting with guests over a mellow lo-fi soundtrack, and the courses mix nigiri with other Japanese small plates, like Hokkaido scallop, futomaki with a soy-cured yolk, and a fried Dungeness crab croquette with béchamel. The counter is roomier than most, and the check lands firmly in special-occasion territory.

entries.pullQuote: Book ahead for the potato waffle benedict, and let someone else order the dutch baby.
entries.blurb: Puffy, sugar-dusted dutch babies made Tilikum Place Café a Belltown brunch fixture, but the supporting cast is the real draw. Think thick-cut bacon, smoked salmon benedict on potato waffles, and bubbling egg skillets layered with gruyere. The small room fills as soon as the doors open, so reserve a table.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the parents to Belltown for a Latin American dinner.
entries.blurb: Lenox serves Latin American food in Belltown, and it works well for a meal with your folks.
For a glass of wine in Belltown that feels like a step up from the usual bar, Neb is a smart pick.

entries.pullQuote: Save the kaiseki menu for an occasion, and savor the sushi courses most.
entries.blurb: Near the Space Needle, where most restaurants disappoint, wa'z quietly serves an excellent kaiseki menu on beautiful dinnerware. The eight courses change monthly but usually include soup, a generous piece of wagyu, and terrific sushi, often brightened with yuzu and mirin. Flavors lean subtle rather than flashy. It's a special-occasion check.

entries.pullQuote: A dependable Belltown Italian dining room for a relaxed weeknight dinner.
entries.blurb: Anyone in Belltown looking for a sit-down Italian meal can head to Assaggio Ristorante.

entries.pullQuote: Get a croissant and peel it apart like a cinnamon roll.
entries.blurb: Belltown's La Parisienne French Bakery makes plenty of tarts and pastries, but the croissants deserve your full attention. Their thick layers unravel in spirals, with a light yeasty flavor, gentle sweetness, and a toasty, sturdy base. It's inexpensive and opens early, so it fits a regular morning routine.

entries.pullQuote: Late Italian in Belltown for when a bar menu just won't do.
entries.blurb: Cotto Belltown serves Italian food and keeps the kitchen going late, which counts for a lot around here.

entries.pullQuote: Order the doughnuts with mascarpone for the table and break the ice.
entries.blurb: Lola brings Greek cooking to Belltown in a room that lands right between casual and upscale, which makes it ideal for having a new partner meet your parents. Brunch calls for the seasonal scramble, and dinner calls for the lamb burger. Then get the cinnamon doughnuts, which come with vanilla bean mascarpone and a fruit compote, and eat one in a single bite.
Belltown gets a dose of Thai cooking at Bangrak Market.

entries.pullQuote: Reserve the big round table, order the brûléed mac and cheese, and share.
entries.blurb: Dinner at Shaker + Spear feels a bit like eating in a very nice home goods showroom, in the best way. The seafood is strong, the staff is sharp and warm, and one round table seats eight if you're bringing a group. Order the prawns in Old Bay butter, the parmesan truffle fries, the charred sprouts, and that torched mac and cheese, then move next door to Pennyroyal for cocktails.

entries.pullQuote: Come at sunset, when the view over Elliott Bay does most of the work.
entries.blurb: Inside the Edgewater Hotel on the waterfront, Six Seven Restaurant is all about the scenery, with big windows and a deck right over the water. The Northwest menu leans on seafood, and happy hour is the low-commitment way to soak it all in.

entries.pullQuote: Dress up, order a dry-aged steak, and let the tableside show unfold.
entries.blurb: Dim lights, live piano, and servers working tableside carts make El Gaucho the old-school supper club Belltown never outgrew. Get a dry-aged cut with a Caesar tossed right in front of you. Bring a fat budget, since this is a special-occasion check through and through.

entries.pullQuote: Seafood up top in Belltown, best saved for a clear evening.
entries.blurb: For seafood with rooftop seating in Belltown, MARKET at the Park is the move.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap, early coffee in Belltown, plus a rooftop to drink it on.
entries.blurb: Early risers in Belltown can grab inexpensive coffee at The Brim Coffee Shop, which also has a rooftop for sipping it.

entries.pullQuote: Come for seafood and stay for the view over the water.
entries.blurb: Seafood and outdoor seating with a view pull a crowd into AQUA by El Gaucho, a polished Belltown spot.

entries.pullQuote: Swing by after work for crab dip, cauliflower, and a round of cocktails.
entries.blurb: Before trading work clothes for sweatpants, stop into Black Bottle in Belltown for a drink. The menu runs long, covering Korean fried chicken bites, spicy cauliflower, and a cheesy Dungeness crab dip, so you can mix it up on every visit. There's a happy hour.

entries.pullQuote: Settle into a dark corner and order something stirred, strong, and classic.
entries.blurb: A dark, grown-up Belltown bar, Rob Roy takes cocktails seriously without getting precious about them. Happy hour is the smart way in, and the bartenders are as comfortable with the classics as with their own inventions.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the pricey entrees and order the margherita with a pasta on the side.
entries.blurb: Blue neon under the bar and champagne bottles as decor make Cinque Terre Ristorante feel a bit like a hotel lobby. Ignore that, because the Neapolitan pies are the real deal, with a charred, crackly crust and a balanced layer of San Marzano and mozzarella. Round things out with casarecce tossed with pesto and ricotta, or boar sugo over rigatoni, and leave the main courses alone.

entries.pullQuote: A late Belltown sushi spot with a happy hour worth planning around.
entries.blurb: Belltown's Wasabi Sushi & Izakaya serves sushi and izakaya plates late into the night, and the discounted hour is a strong reason to stop in.

title: Ballard
dek: Where to eat and drink in Ballard, from a weeknight to a night you bothered to dress for.
intro:
Ballard eats well if you let it. AA Sushi and Cardoon cover the cravings, and the walks between them are short enough to stay hungry.

Same craving does not get to take over the page. A neighborhood should feel like a week of dinners, not one cuisine copied down the block.

entries.pullQuote: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.
entries.blurb: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.

entries.pullQuote: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.
entries.blurb: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.

entries.pullQuote: Organic baguettes, levain and rye, baked in Ballard since 2000.
entries.blurb: Pick up a classic baguette or the pain au levain, both made with organic flour. The Ballard shop is open Wednesday to Sunday, 9 to 6.

entries.pullQuote: Griddled corned beef with mint and pickled cabbage, from a Momofuku alum.
entries.blurb: Order the Mean: thick griddled corned beef, house yellow mustard, pickled red cabbage and fresh mint on a challah bun. It comes with the salt-and-pepper potato skins.

entries.pullQuote: Aussie meat pies, rugby and a raised Ballard patio in an old library.
entries.blurb: Order the pie, beans, chips and gravy, an Aussie meat pie with Heinz beans, and take it to the raised patio over Market Street. Rugby and Premier League are on the screens.

entries.pullQuote: Expect a line, a pile of tasting spoons, and flavors you won't find elsewhere.
entries.blurb: The Portland-born Salt & Straw brings its oddball, seasonal scoops to Ballard, and the counter stays open late. Staff hand out samples freely, which helps when the monthly specials get weird.

entries.pullQuote: Hawaiian bar food and a kitchen open past eleven make an easy Ballard nightcap.
entries.blurb: Hawaiian plates and a late-running kitchen make Pono Ranch a handy stop on any Ballard bar crawl.

entries.pullQuote: Skee-ball, buffalo wings, and a mango slushie if the machine is kind.
entries.blurb: King's Hardware is a dim Ballard bar with taxidermy on the walls, baskets of buffalo wings, and two Skee-Ball lanes that turn a round into a score. Slushies rotate. Hope for mango lemonade, then roll anyway. Weekends fill the room without tipping into a shout. Play a game before the second basket arrives, and leave the coaster lecture to a lounge that scheduled its lighting.

entries.pullQuote: Get the korma pie and accept every extra pour of gravy offered.
entries.blurb: From the folks behind Beast & Cleaver, The Little Beast looks like a regular British pub on Ballard's main drag until the food arrives. The lamb korma pie comes buried in gravy, the currywurst sausage roll pairs well with a Pimm's cup, and the charred pork chop with grilled nectarines is a standout. Scotch eggs and sing-along rock round out the evening.

entries.pullQuote: Excellent nigiri at casual prices, and you can usually walk right in with friends.
entries.blurb: AA Sushi in Ballard makes a casual sushi night feel like a splurge without the bill. Small groups can usually stroll in and sit down fast in a plain but comfortable room. Cover the table in nigiri, rolls, and miso soup, and pay attention to the rice, which holds together and stays just warm enough to soften a slice of yellowtail belly.

entries.pullQuote: Order the croissant, then come back tomorrow for another one.
entries.blurb: The morning line at Rosellini's tells you everything about where Ballard gets its pastry. The baguette and cinnamon-swirled coffee cake are excellent, but the croissant is the reason to come, with shattering layers, deep butter flavor, and a crumb that springs back when you press it. Get there early, since the doors open before nine.

entries.pullQuote: Ballard's candlelit wood-fired pies prove Seattle belongs in the great pizza conversation.
entries.blurb: Seattle can hold its own as a pizza town, and Delancey is the proof. Start with burrata swimming in pesto or the towering Jersey Salad, then focus on the blistered pies topped with fennel sausage, sweet Walla Walla onions, or kalamatas. The dim room smells like the oven and works for date night or dinner with the family.

entries.pullQuote: Try a matcha latte with banana foam, which tastes better than it sounds.
entries.blurb: A pink La Marzocco anchors the counter at Joie Coffee, a tiny Ballard cafe obsessed with creamy toppings.
