entries.pullQuote: For a proper afternoon tea with all the frills, start your search here.
entries.blurb: Ravenna's Queen Mary Tea Room goes all in on the ritual, with aproned servers passing around tea samples and decor that changes with the seasons. Tiered trays come loaded with things like tiny cups of tomato bisque plus fresh fruit for dragging through clotted cream. There's a gluten-free version that holds its own, and the tea list is huge.

entries.pullQuote: Book ahead for the potato waffle benedict, and let someone else order the dutch baby.
entries.blurb: Puffy, sugar-dusted dutch babies made Tilikum Place Café a Belltown brunch fixture, but the supporting cast is the real draw. Think thick-cut bacon, smoked salmon benedict on potato waffles, and bubbling egg skillets layered with gruyere. The small room fills as soon as the doors open, so reserve a table.

entries.pullQuote: Phinney Ridge locals line up early for loaves and pastries at this bakery.
entries.blurb: Walk in early for inexpensive bread and baked goods in Phinney Ridge at Ben’s Bread Co.

entries.pullQuote: Order a honey lavender latte, claim the window seat, and pretend to work.
entries.blurb: Fram squeezes a lot of fun into a room about the size of a single garage. Lavender lattes sweetened with honey and constantly churning frosé lead the menu, and the fridge holds a good stash of cans and bottles. Strong wifi makes it a natural work spot, though the nearby lake makes a coffee walk awfully tempting.

entries.pullQuote: Try a matcha latte with banana foam, which tastes better than it sounds.
entries.blurb: A pink La Marzocco anchors the counter at Joie Coffee, a tiny Ballard cafe obsessed with creamy toppings. Banana cream on iced matcha or brownie batter foam on a mocha sounds sugary, but the drinks stay surprisingly balanced. Purists can order a strong Vietnamese coffee, though the tiramisu and strawberry foams are more fun.

entries.pullQuote: Hide out upstairs with a latte and the bacon, egg, and Beecher's sandwich.
entries.blurb: Konvene Coffee Cafe is tucked upstairs inside a QFC. The baristas are friendly and steam milk beautifully. Seating is limited and there are no outlets, so plan on a short work session. Hungry visitors should order the bacon and egg sandwich with Beecher's cheese and aioli on brioche.

entries.pullQuote: Get the Italian sub, add a breakfast sandwich, and bring patience.
entries.blurb: The owners once ran Lyon's Grocery in Queen Anne, and that pedigree shows in every sandwich at Otherside Market & Deli in Eastlake. The Italian sub piles on ham with pepperoncini and a hit of red wine vinegar, while breakfast sandwiches arrive gooey on Backyard bagels. Even a plain turkey and cheese on wheat is great here.

Glo’s moved off its old Olive Way corner but kept the neon, the stone walls, and the mid-century charm. The wait still stretches past an hour on weekends, and it still pays off. Expect hash browns with a shattering golden crust, scallion and garlic scrambles, and a tangy homemade corned beef hash.

entries.pullQuote: An early Capitol Hill breakfast here makes an easy win with visiting parents.
entries.blurb: Opening early for breakfast and brunch, Harry’s Fine Foods serves New American cooking that suits a meal with the folks.

entries.pullQuote: Go on a weekday morning and claim a swivel stool at the counter.
entries.blurb: Every neighborhood deserves a diner as cheerful as Geraldine's Counter, where the coffee refills never stop coming. Take a window seat, soak up the Rainier Avenue light, and work through crisp french toast and thick-cut bacon. Weekend waits run long, so a quieter weekday is the smarter play.

entries.pullQuote: Get takeout from Lil Red's when the week calls for Jamaican comfort food.
entries.blurb: Lil Red's in Columbia City cooks Jamaican barbecue and soul food that works as a reset button on a stressful week. Every plate from this kitchen leans hard into comfort, and it's still a top takeout pick. It opens early, too.

entries.pullQuote: Get the licorice caramel latte and dunk a cardamom rose cookie in it.
entries.blurb: This tiny Ballard cafe pulls Kuma espresso with Chinese and German touches, and its oat lattes come out impossibly silky. A salty licorice caramel drink brings a gentle anise edge. Sunlight pours through the windows at Cardoon, the snug corner seats are surprisingly comfortable, and the doors open early.

entries.pullQuote: Order the plain croissant, a steady classic that gets every essential right.
entries.blurb: The French Guys works out of a little stone cottage on Capitol Hill that looks lifted from a storybook. Their plain croissant isn't the flakiest or richest around, but it's buttery, crunchy, and dependable in a way you'll come to count on. It opens early, and prices are gentle.

entries.pullQuote: Start a Fremont morning with an inexpensive bagel before the crowds wake up.
entries.blurb: Early Fremont mornings stay cheap and well fed thanks to Backyard Bagel.

title: Late-Night Eats
dek: Kitchens and bars still going at 11pm or later.
intro:
Kitchens and bars still going at 11pm or later. Chez Phinney and Dead Line are still going when the rest of Phinney Ridge, Pioneer Square, West Seattle has turned into porch lights.

Hunger after dark is a different animal. These are the kitchens and bars that still take it seriously.

entries.pullQuote: Eight dollars, a putter, and thirty-two taps in South Lake Union.
entries.blurb: Flatstick Pub built a mini-golf course into a South Lake Union bar. A round costs eight dollars, the floor is big enough for a group that cannot choose a restaurant, and 32 taps end the argument about beer. Order the brick-oven pizza instead of stopping at onion rings. Keep the putter away from anyone's face. The person who loses can buy the next round without a meeting about it.

entries.pullQuote: Use it for happy hour and stick around for the hourly drink wheel.
entries.blurb: Von's 1000Spirits lives up to its name with a huge bar and a long list of bottles. The sourdough pizza and pasta are solid and the cocktails are better, but this is mostly a happy hour or post-day-drinking lunch move. Every hour they spin a wheel to pick the drink special, and it stays open late.

Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

The 5 Point Cafe faces the five-way at Tilikum Place, and the doors have been open since 1929. It is the oldest bar in Belltown and also a cafe that can serve breakfast as a nightcap. The city already filed it under dive: a long counter, regulars who do not surrender a stool, and no interest in a redesign. Eat something that can survive a second beer. Then stay later than the plan you walked in with.

entries.pullQuote: Thick handmade tortillas and that chorizo, potato, and cactus filling are the move.
entries.blurb: Carmelo's Tacos presses its own hefty tortillas and fills them with well-marinated carne asada or a chorizo, potato, and nopal mix that sticks with you. Burrito people should know the cheese gets a quick sear on the griddle before it goes in. It's cheap, it's fast, and the Capitol Hill counter keeps going late.

entries.pullQuote: Natural wine nerds, this is your clubhouse, deep cuts and murky pours included.
entries.blurb: Remember the Juice Club pop-up? Its crew now runs Otherworld, a Capitol Hill natural wine bar built for glou-glou devotees. Prices hang on a deli-style felt board, the shelves are lined with bottles sporting arty labels, and the music runs funky and obscure. Settle in with small glasses of something cloudy, and know the night runs long here.

entries.pullQuote: Fremont's go-to for watching the game with a big, loud group.
entries.blurb: Bring the whole crew to Petoskey's Sports Bar in Fremont for the game, bar food, and a late close.

title: Big Group Dinners That Don't Suck
dek: Breweries, halls, and the louder rooms.
intro:

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Greenwood, South Lake Union, Georgetown will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Panko-crusted cod and Cajun fried shrimp at a Fremont dive since 1981.
entries.blurb: Order the fish and chips: thin Pacific cod in a peppery, garlicky panko crust. Add the Cajun fried shrimp and eat on the deck; the pub is 21 and over.

entries.pullQuote: Beer pong, trivia, and a karaoke contest for anyone pretending to attend UW.
entries.blurb: Finn Maccools is the Irish pub on the Ave where a night arrives with a student activity sheet: strong wells, beer pong, trivia, and a karaoke contest. The crowd is mostly collegiate, plus anyone willing to blend in. Walk past it on University Way after dark and you missed the block's loudest room. Pizza can wait on the table. The contest is why that stool is still warm.

entries.pullQuote: Show up as a crowd, find a screen, and keep the tab cheap.
entries.blurb: Cheap drinks, games on the TVs, and room for a big group make Earl's on the Ave a U District standby that stays open late.

entries.pullQuote: Rally a big group here to watch the game and eat bar food.
entries.blurb: Game days in Belltown mean a crowd at Buckley's, a sports bar with plenty of room for groups and a kitchen open late.
Big groups can spread out over a round of beers at Snapshot Brewing, a brewery in Greenwood.

entries.pullQuote: House beers and plenty of tables when your whole crew hits the market.
entries.blurb: In the market, Old Stove Brewing pours its own beer and has room for a big group.

entries.pullQuote: Wild sours, hazy IPAs, and a pastrami truck out front settle every group debate.
entries.blurb: The tap list here swings from peanut butter and jelly sours to turtle stout to fruit-loaded IPAs, so nobody needs a plan. A big patio sits on a busy Maple Leaf corner and makes for a long, summery session. For food, the Sammich truck parked outside does a pastrami sandwich that's the move. When friends are coming from opposite ends of the city, meet at Project 9 Brewing Co.

entries.pullQuote: Call here when you need a last-minute birthday table for a dozen friends.
entries.blurb: The menu at Re:public dresses up comfort food, with burgers, Nashville hot chicken sandwiches, and mac and cheese loaded with prawns and pork belly. It's more about the mood than the cooking, especially in summer when the garage doors roll up. Groups can usually claim a section of the bar with little notice, the kitchen stays open late, and there's a happy hour too.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the sunny-afternoon crowds and come after dark for the lit-up lake.
entries.blurb: Nautical decor and big water views make The White Swan Public House look like a tourist trap, but it mostly sidesteps the clichés. Stick with the seafood and you'll eat well. Warm afternoons get packed, so come after sundown, when tables open up and party boats drift across Lake Union. Happy hour and big groups are both easy here.

entries.pullQuote: Bocce, a boot of lager, and bratwurst in a Capitol Hill hall.
entries.blurb: Rhein Haus is a Capitol Hill beer hall of long wooden tables, bratwurst, and bocce played hard enough to sour a friendship. Lager arrives by the liter in a glass boot. Pretzels come with beer cheese, and warm months set the slushie machines spinning. The bathroom line can outlast a sitcom episode. The crowd is young and loud, which is the recommendation. Claim a lane before the hall claims your whole night.

entries.pullQuote: Come for hockey on every screen and a plate of poutine for the table.
entries.blurb: Hockey is always on at The Angry Beaver, a Greenwood sports bar where poutine is the move. It handles big groups without fuss.

entries.pullQuote: Bring takeout barbecue and spend a long afternoon at the picnic tables.
entries.blurb: Fremont Brewing is daytime drinking at its most generous, with a sprawling patio, long communal tables, and free pretzels. Two infused Randall taps rotate constantly, so there's always something new to try. Outside food is welcome, which means a sack of Roro BBQ and a flight make a great Fremont outing.

entries.pullQuote: Gather a big group, order pints of Space Dust, and settle in.
entries.blurb: Big tables, a long tap list, and Space Dust IPA at the source make Elysian Brewing - Capitol Hill a simple yes for groups. Happy hour helps, and the pub keeps pouring late.

entries.pullQuote: A Capitol Hill pub that stays open until 2 and skips the cocktail lecture.
entries.blurb: The Roanoke is a Capitol Hill pub with a dive's closing time and a screen somewhere if the game is on. It runs until 2, the lights stay low, and the order is a beer rather than a ten-ingredient drink. Take a stool if you came alone. Let the table get loud if you did not. It is the neighborhood tavern for a night that needs neither a reservation nor an occasion.

entries.pullQuote: Post Alley hides the sofa, the Spam birdcage, and a cardboard drinks list.
entries.blurb: White Horse Tavern sits in Post Alley, which is why market crowds walk past it. The ceiling holds photos, paintings, umbrellas, and a birdcage with a can of Spam inside. Drinks are listed in marker on cardboard. Order Bulls Blood if you want port mixed with dry champagne, then take the red velvet sofa. Three friends on a weekend is the right headcount. A party of twelve will not fit, and should not try.

title: Walk-In Friendly
dek: Counters, cafes, bakeries, and other places built for showing up.
intro:
Counters, cafes, bakeries, and other places built for showing up. Anchorhead Coffee and Bottega Gabriele are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Downtown, Pioneer Square, Ballard without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Downtown, Pioneer Square, Ballard will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

entries.pullQuote: Get the steamed barbecue pork bao and eat it walking through the stalls.
entries.blurb: Swing by in the late morning, before the market fully wakes up, and you'll catch the crew at Mee Sum Pastry folding potstickers and pinching shumai. Grab an assortment and snack your way through Pike Place. It's all good, but the steamed pork hum bao is the order regulars make, and it's open early and inexpensive.

Sesame hoagie rolls are crunchy and chewy, bacon is chopped into small bits, and cold cuts are shaved impossibly thin. The bacon, egg and cheese is on a poppy seed bagel. There's an arcade room next door for pinball after lunch.

entries.pullQuote: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.
entries.blurb: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Thanksgiving turkey sandwich and add tater tots for dunking.
entries.blurb: Valhalla Sandwiches in Greenwood manages to go big without getting sloppy. The sandwiches come on sturdy telera rolls with fillings like blackened shrimp and chorizo, chicken with sweet-hot mustard and slaw, or turkey with stuffing, cranberry, and rosemary aioli. Tater tots with chipotle mayo are a must, and the whole thing is inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: A no-fuss Fremont counter for a cheap burger without a reservation.
entries.blurb: Walk in, order at the counter, and Uneeda Burger will hand you an inexpensive burger in Fremont.

entries.pullQuote: Brave the line of tourists for a cup of that famous mac and cheese.
entries.blurb: The nutty, sharp Flagship cheddar from Beecher's Handmade Cheese is in every grocery store in town, but the Pike Place Market shop is where it all gets made. Expect a line packed with curd-sampling tourists at lunch. The reward is a creamy mac and cheese that once made Oprah's list of favorite things, and it's inexpensive.

entries.pullQuote: Order the adobada tacos with grilled pineapple and you've made the right call.
entries.blurb: The Broadway taco counter in a building shared with a tattoo shop stopped being a secret long ago, and Tacos Chukis earned the crowds. The house adobada tacos stack marinated grilled pork with avocado salsa, cilantro, onion, and a seared slab of pineapple. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, and it's an ideal stop before a night out.

entries.pullQuote: Order the croissant, then come back tomorrow for another one.
entries.blurb: The morning line at Rosellini's tells you everything about where Ballard gets its pastry. The baguette and cinnamon-swirled coffee cake are excellent, but the croissant is the reason to come, with shattering layers, deep butter flavor, and a crumb that springs back when you press it. Get there early, since the doors open before nine.

entries.pullQuote: Phinney Ridge locals line up early for loaves and pastries at this bakery.
entries.blurb: Walk in early for inexpensive bread and baked goods in Phinney Ridge at Ben’s Bread Co.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap Italian sandwiches in Greenwood, no reservation needed, just show up hungry.
entries.blurb: Fortuna Bottega makes inexpensive Italian sandwiches at a walk-up Greenwood counter.

entries.pullQuote: Order more empanadas than you think you need, especially the creamed spinach.
entries.blurb: Over in Ballard, Maria Luisa Empanadas turns out tender pastries stuffed with meats, cheeses, and vegetables, plus a chimichurri you'll want to bottle. The garage-style room has high-tops for a quick lunch, and takeout is easy even for a crowd. Picking a favorite is hard, but the creamed spinach and the tangy chorizo lead the pack.

entries.pullQuote: The corned beef reuben here is the benchmark for every deli in town.
entries.blurb: Look for the huge corned beef sign over the Denny Triangle and you've found Market House Meats. The shop has fed office workers and early construction crews since the forties, and the griddle is always sizzling. That tender, salty corned beef goes into a reuben you'll measure every other one against. It's inexpensive, quick, and open early.

entries.pullQuote: Order the salted graham in an affogato and forget about the weather.
entries.blurb: Whimsical signs out front hint at what's inside Marmalade, a Fremont gelato shop that might spoil you for the rest of the city. The gelato is spun fresh and airy, and the flavors get creative without getting silly. White chocolate tastes rich and buttery, salted graham is nutty and layered, and strawberry lemonade sorbetto is as smooth as soft serve. Go big with the Americano cup or get a scoop drowned in espresso.

entries.pullQuote: Get the Italian sub, add a breakfast sandwich, and bring patience.
entries.blurb: The owners once ran Lyon's Grocery in Queen Anne, and that pedigree shows in every sandwich at Otherside Market & Deli in Eastlake. The Italian sub piles on ham with pepperoncini and a hit of red wine vinegar, while breakfast sandwiches arrive gooey on Backyard bagels. Even a plain turkey and cheese on wheat is great here.

entries.pullQuote: Cheap scoops in Wallingford, no planning required, just show up hungry.
entries.blurb: Inexpensive ice cream in Wallingford is the whole pitch at Many Bennies, and you can just walk in.

entries.pullQuote: Order the matcha parfait with cake on top and call it lunch.
entries.blurb: After a rough morning, sometimes the fix is sitting alone with soft serve in a waffle cone crowned with a whole slice of cake. Nana's Green Tea, a matcha-everything Japanese cafe downtown, is happy to make that your midday meal.

entries.pullQuote: This gluten-free Filipino fried chicken is crispier than nearly anything else in town.
entries.blurb: The Chicken Supply dredges its Filipino fried chicken in tapioca, rice flour, and potato starch, and that celiac-friendly coating is exactly why it's so good. Thigh skin crackles like a chip, and the skewers of white meat stay remarkably juicy. Seating is limited to a handful of tables in the small Phinney Ridge room. Prices stay pleasantly low.

title: Bring The Parents
dek: The spendier dining rooms, when the visit needs a tablecloth mood.
intro:
The spendier dining rooms, when the visit needs a tablecloth mood. AA Sushi and Cafe Lolo are where the night should feel like you left the house for a reason.

The test is simple: can you hear each other, and is the food good enough that the check feels like part of the night instead of the ending.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the parents for Lao food that feels comforting and still like a real night out.
entries.blurb: Capitol Hill's Taurus Ox cooks Lao food with real heat and funk, and it rewards a table that's willing to share. Order sticky rice no matter what. The room works as well for a date as it does for dinner with your folks.

entries.pullQuote: Get the pomodoro with burrata and leave space for the ricotta crostata.
entries.blurb: Inside Pike Place Market, Pasta Casalinga turns out handmade bowls that would hold their own in Italy. The rotating menu pulls from ocean, garden, and farm, think rigatoni with lamb and juniper ragu or spaghettoni tossed in kale pesto. The best bowl is the simplest one, pomodoro topped with a cool spoonful of burrata. If the ricotta chocolate crostata is on, order it, and bring your parents.

entries.pullQuote: Order the margherita flatbread and a cocktail for a quiet, easy date.
entries.blurb: Few people seem to know about Single Shot Kitchen & Saloon, which gives a date here some built-in novelty. It's a single handsome room, marble bar included, with candles on every table, oddly calm given the noise of Pike-Pine outside. title: The Bar List
dek: Cocktails, wine, and the dives worth standing in.
intro:
Cocktails, wine, and the dives worth standing in. Start at Chez Phinney. If the room is right, you will not need a second plan.

Order one drink the way the bar wants it, then decide if you are staying. A well-made classic beats a menu pun. Food is welcome. It is not the cover charge.

entries.blurb: At first glance Stampede Cocktail Club reads as a vintage-leaning cocktail bar, until you round a corner and come face to face with a dinosaur head hung against floral wallpaper. The drinks are excellent, including a blueberry mule and a passionfruit margarita with pineapple, and the steamed dumplings come from Little Ting's. It's fun for a date and open late.
Erik Hakkinen's Belltown bar leans on cognac and calvados, and it's open until 1 or 2am every night.

entries.pullQuote: Panko-crusted cod and Cajun fried shrimp at a Fremont dive since 1981.
entries.blurb: Order the fish and chips: thin Pacific cod in a peppery, garlicky panko crust. Add the Cajun fried shrimp and eat on the deck; the pub is 21 and over.

entries.pullQuote: Eight dollars, a putter, and thirty-two taps in South Lake Union.
entries.blurb: Flatstick Pub built a mini-golf course into a South Lake Union bar. A round costs eight dollars, the floor is big enough for a group that cannot choose a restaurant, and 32 taps end the argument about beer. Order the brick-oven pizza instead of stopping at onion rings. Keep the putter away from anyone's face. The person who loses can buy the next round without a meeting about it.

entries.pullQuote: Long communal tables and liters of German beer make group nights easy.
entries.blurb: Near Seattle Center, Queen Anne Beerhall is a roomy German-style beer hall with shared tables and plenty of space for a crowd. That early drink deal is a solid deal, and the bar keeps pouring well past eleven, which helps after a game or concert next door.

entries.pullQuote: Open since 1929, and still pouring when Belltown has gone home.
entries.blurb: The 5 Point Cafe faces the five-way at Tilikum Place, and the doors have been open since 1929. It is the oldest bar in Belltown and also a cafe that can serve breakfast as a nightcap. The city already filed it under dive: a long counter, regulars who do not surrender a stool, and no interest in a redesign. Eat something that can survive a second beer. Then stay later than the plan you walked in with.

entries.pullQuote: Rally a big group here to watch the game and eat bar food.
entries.blurb: Game days in Belltown mean a crowd at Buckley's, a sports bar with plenty of room for groups and a kitchen open late.

entries.pullQuote: Come at happy hour, when the chips, olives, and nuts arrive free with drinks.
entries.blurb: Dead Line is small, dark, and polished, with shelves of bottles so tall the bartenders need a rolling ladder. Beyond the serious cocktails, the kitchen turns out South American small plates like brisket arepas and squash al pastor tacos. The pre-dinner window is a steal, and the bar pours past eleven.

entries.pullQuote: Order the Lychee Blossom and bring a first date up to the loft.
entries.blurb: Most trips to Biang Biang Noodles end face-first in a bowl of mala beef, but look up next time. Behind red velvet curtains sits Paper Fan Cocktail Bar, a snug loft dressed with ornate lamps and delicate fans. A few of the tea-based drinks lean medicinal, though the Lychee Blossom, made with gin, green tea, and lemon, drinks bright and easy. It fills up fast, so reserve ahead for a first date.

entries.pullQuote: Order the pork belly burnt ends and a whiskey, then stay for another round.
entries.blurb: Climb the stairs above the market and you'll find Radiator Whiskey, a small, dark room with a deep whiskey list and food built to absorb it. Think burnt ends, tots smothered in gravy with a fried egg, and marrow bones set up for a luge. Reserve ahead for the smoked pig's head, though landing a table on a Friday is usually painless.

entries.pullQuote: Georgetown night owls should keep this cocktail lounge in their back pocket.
entries.blurb: Late-night drinkers in Georgetown land at 1988 Cocktail Lounge for mixed drinks that keep coming well after eleven.

entries.pullQuote: Self-pour wine machines and late-night dance music make this the north end's best wine stop.
entries.blurb: Hand over a card, grab an empty glass, and work your way through the self-serve taps at Chez Phinney. Snack on house chocolate truffles plus Michou Deli dips between pours. By day the room looks like a Parisian cafe inside an airport terminal, but after dark the music gets loud and nobody's rushing you out.
For a glass of wine in Belltown that feels like a step up from the usual bar, Neb is a smart pick.
Donna's pours drinks on the Hill and makes the cut among the neighborhood's better bars.

entries.pullQuote: Sit at the bar with champagne and a board of charcuterie.
entries.blurb: When you want Paris without the flight, Le Caviste delivers a candlelit bar, a glass of bubbly, and excellent cured meats. It suits a quick bite before a date or a solo unwind after a rough workday. The bar pours past eleven.

entries.pullQuote: Band stickers, sunk leather stools, and cheap beer when a band is loading in.
entries.blurb: Blue Moon Tavern is the U District bar for cheap beer and whatever band is hauling amps through the door. Stickers from old shows cover the walls, the stools have collapsed into their leather, and the booths look sawed from a backyard tree. Sit down if you like a room that remembers its own concerts. Walk on if you wanted a host stand. The Ave has plenty of those, and none of them have this many stickers.

entries.pullQuote: Fremont's go-to for watching the game with a big, loud group.
entries.blurb: Bring the whole crew to Petoskey's Sports Bar in Fremont for the game, bar food, and a late close.
Bar food and drinks are what you'll find at Slim Goody in Ballard.

entries.pullQuote: South Park's double tavern burger, charred, and better at the bar than in the car.
entries.blurb: Loretta's Northwesterner is the South Park dive organized around a double tavern burger: charred, stacked, special sauce, pickles, cheese, onion, and nothing clever after that. Fries and a beer at the bar are the indoor plan. The back patio is the move when the weather remembers the south end. Carry one out only if you are walking a short block. The sear loses the argument inside a car.

entries.pullQuote: Wall-to-wall coolers, a deep tap list, and a crowd that treats it like a living room.
entries.blurb: Chuck's Hop Shop pairs a long run of taps with coolers packed with bottles and cans. You can linger past eleven.

entries.pullQuote: Pinball, a fair well drink, and four-player Pac-Man in Fremont.
entries.blurb: Add-a-Ball is a Fremont arcade for people 21 and over. Beer is priced like a neighborhood bar, and the wells do not taste like melted ice. Four-player Pac-Man has settled nights here. Killer Queen will unsettle them if anyone actually knows the rules. On Saturday evenings, Good Shape parks a pizza pop-up beside the machines, so dinner never requires a coat. Stay until the last ball drains.

entries.pullQuote: Pineapple on the fried fish, a painkiller, and a booth big enough for Uno.
entries.blurb: Bait Shop cannot pick between a nautical dive and a tiki shack, so the Capitol Hill room does both. Pineapple or bacon can land on the fried fish, and the fries have their own local following. Frozen drinks change by the day. Learn the painkiller by name: rum, pineapple, coconut, orange, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Take a big booth, deal a hand of Uno, and leave the amaro lecture for a different door on the hill.

title: Best Fun & Dive Bars
dek: Dives, pinball, mini golf, karaoke, and the bars that would rather be loud.
intro:
Cocktail rooms with a leather menu live on the other drinks list. This page is for sticky floors, a game you can lose, and a mic nobody booked. The 5 Point Cafe has been pouring in Belltown since 1929. Blue Moon still wears its band stickers. Add-a-Ball and Flatstick Pub are where the night keeps score.

Sing at Finn Maccools or Marco Polo when the room is already loud. Eat the tavern burger at Loretta's Northwesterner, on the back patio if South Park is warm. At White Horse Tavern, Bulls Blood is port cut with dry champagne, written in marker on cardboard.

Order the pie, beans, chips and gravy, an Aussie meat pie with Heinz beans, and take it to the raised patio over Market Street. Rugby and Premier League are on the screens.

entries.pullQuote: Lower Queen Anne karaoke, priced like a dive, and open until 2.
entries.blurb: Ozzie's is a Lower Queen Anne dive with karaoke and an American kitchen, and the lights stay on until 2. Prices sit at the cheap end on purpose. Pick a song you can finish, stand where people will clap, and skip the night if nobody in the group will sing. A plainer pub can sell you a beer anywhere on Queen Anne. This room only earns the walk once the microphone is switched on.
Hawaiian plates and a late-running kitchen make Pono Ranch a handy stop on any Ballard bar crawl.

entries.pullQuote: Beer pong, trivia, and a karaoke contest for anyone pretending to attend UW.
entries.blurb: Finn Maccools is the Irish pub on the Ave where a night arrives with a student activity sheet: strong wells, beer pong, trivia, and a karaoke contest. The crowd is mostly collegiate, plus anyone willing to blend in. Walk past it on University Way after dark and you missed the block's loudest room. Pizza can wait on the table. The contest is why that stool is still warm.

entries.pullQuote: Skee-ball, buffalo wings, and a mango slushie if the machine is kind.
entries.blurb: King's Hardware is a dim Ballard bar with taxidermy on the walls, baskets of buffalo wings, and two Skee-Ball lanes that turn a round into a score. Slushies rotate. Hope for mango lemonade, then roll anyway. Weekends fill the room without tipping into a shout. Play a game before the second basket arrives, and leave the coaster lecture to a lounge that scheduled its lighting.

entries.pullQuote: Bocce, a boot of lager, and bratwurst in a Capitol Hill hall.
entries.blurb: Rhein Haus is a Capitol Hill beer hall of long wooden tables, bratwurst, and bocce played hard enough to sour a friendship. Lager arrives by the liter in a glass boot. Pretzels come with beer cheese, and warm months set the slushie machines spinning. The bathroom line can outlast a sitcom episode. The crowd is young and loud, which is the recommendation. Claim a lane before the hall claims your whole night.

title: Gusto's 25
dek: Twenty-five dining rooms for when dinner should feel like an event.
intro:
Twenty-five rooms for when dinner should feel like an event, spread across the city so you do not eat the same night twice. AA Sushi and Bé Mi are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Ballard, Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Ballard, Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.

It sits inside a historic homestead, which makes the setting feel special without getting stuffy.

entries.pullQuote: Skip the broth and go all in on a bowl of saucy aburasoba.
entries.blurb: Kajiken specializes in aburasoba, a brothless style of ramen where springy noodles get tossed in a rich sauce at the bottom of the bowl. The Capitol Hill shop keeps things casual.

The highlight is the uni cart, which delivers a rich sea urchin hand roll like a treat from a street vendor. Chefs explain the story behind every piece, and the sake pairing keeps flowing all night.

entries.pullQuote: Get the korma pie and accept every extra pour of gravy offered.
entries.blurb: From the folks behind Beast & Cleaver, The Little Beast looks like a regular British pub on Ballard's main drag until the food arrives. The lamb korma pie comes buried in gravy, the currywurst sausage roll pairs well with a Pimm's cup, and the charred pork chop with grilled nectarines is a standout. Scotch eggs and sing-along rock round out the evening.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the parents here for a Turkish dinner that feels like an occasion.
entries.blurb: For a dressed-up Turkish meal in Phinney Ridge, Ada's Restaurant & Bar carries a special-occasion check that works well with family in tow.

entries.pullQuote: Order the daily bento and plan on skipping the rest of your afternoon.
entries.blurb: Midafternoon on a weekday, this Fremont lunch spot is still full of people who clearly cleared their calendars. At Made in House, the bento changes daily and brings bulgogi, a jammy egg, springy japchae, and tempura kale that cracks apart at first bite. Salmon kimbop gets rolled fresh each day, and the shortbread bar tastes like a homemade candy bar.

entries.pullQuote: Order the kalua pig and cabbage, and get it in a quesadilla.
entries.blurb: Maple Leaf's Kona Kitchen feels like a roadside stop on Oahu, with island memorabilia on the walls and squishy booths to sink into. The mai tais are strong, the spam musubi is reliable, and the loco moco comes smothered in gravy with your pick of rice and protein. Smoky kalua pig with cabbage is the real highlight, and the kitchen runs from breakfast through late night.

entries.pullQuote: Order the phở hà nội and drop that raw yolk right in.
entries.blurb: It looks like any strip-mall Vietnamese spot in Greenwood, but Miss Pho cooks well above the setting. Phở hà nội comes brimming with broth and topped with a raw egg yolk, great stirred in or spooned over each bite of noodles and beef shank. The grilled chicken is fragrant with lemongrass, and vegetarians eat just as well here.

entries.pullQuote: This is the teriyaki to settle any argument about the city's signature takeout.
entries.blurb: Teriyaki is a Seattle invention, and Rainier Teriyaki in Mount Baker is the standard everyone else gets measured against. The chicken comes off the grill with a smoky char and a glaze that caramelizes on the edges. Little touches seal it, like iceberg salad packed on the side so it stays crisp, blistered gingery gyoza, and extra sauce tucked in without asking. Takeout comes together fast without slipping.

entries.blurb: The Fremont room feels like a boxcar diner shrunk down by a tiny-house builder, and Seattle Biscuit Company serves breakfast all day. Biscuits anchor everything, and they are excellent, whether in a sandwich like the peanut butter, apple, and jam Lunch Pail or smothered in classic gravy. Very hungry groups can tackle a huge platter of biscuits and eggs.

entries.pullQuote: Book ahead for the potato waffle benedict, and let someone else order the dutch baby.
entries.blurb: Puffy, sugar-dusted dutch babies made Tilikum Place Café a Belltown brunch fixture, but the supporting cast is the real draw. Think thick-cut bacon, smoked salmon benedict on potato waffles, and bubbling egg skillets layered with gruyere. The small room fills as soon as the doors open, so reserve a table.
Pizza is the main event at Stevie's Famous, a casual spot on Beacon Hill.

entries.pullQuote: Bring the parents to Belltown for a Latin American dinner.
entries.blurb: Lenox serves Latin American food in Belltown, and it works well for a meal with your folks.

entries.pullQuote: Order the belly dip with house chips first, then a crab roll.
entries.blurb: Local Tide makes a case for Seattle seafood beyond salmon and chowder, though it nails those too. At this Fremont counter, the smoked belly dip with thin, house-seasoned chips is a must. Sandwiches are the main event, from the weekend crab roll with lemon mayo and chives to a dover sole take on the Filet-O-Fish. Shrimp toast with pork fat and a happy hour make it easy to come back.
